title: What to know about Wednesday's total solar eclipse
summary: The only total solar eclipse of 2026 will cross the Northern Hemisphere on Wednesday, Aug. 12, with a path of totality across parts of Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain. See when and where it will be visible.
story: The only total solar eclipse of 2026 will have people looking to the skies as darkness falls on its path across part of the Northern Hemisphere on Wednesday.

First, if you've never had the opportunity to see a solar eclipse, what you are watching is the moon passing in front of the sun. It occurs somewhere on Earth about every 18 months, but in any one particular spot on the globe they could happen hundreds of years apart.
Here's what to know about when and where to see the total solar eclipse:
Where will the solar eclipse be visible?
Many of the best places to view totality are not inhabited, like northern Greenland. But western Iceland and northern Spain are also on the path of totality for a peak eclipse experience.
In Spain, they have not experienced a total solar eclipse since 1905.
This animation from NASA shows the path of totality for the eclipse, along with the time when it will cross those areas:

Even though totality will be visible in only a few populated regions, a partial solar eclipse will be visible in a much wider area. About 230 million people will be able to see 90% totality, according to population data from the Center for International Earth Science Information Network at Columbia University.
Most major cities in Europe will see at least 90% totality, including Madrid, London and Paris.

Even some of North America will get a chance to see a partial solar eclipse, though it won't be nearly as impressive as when the U.S. got to see a total eclipse in 2024. The best place to see it in the U.S. is in Fairbanks, Alaska, where it will reach 37% totality.
Boston will see 16% totality, while New York City will see about 9% totality, Toronto will see about 8% and Philadelphia will see 7%.
What time will the eclipse happen?
Since the eclipse is crossing just the northern part of the globe, the path of totality will be fairly short from start to finish, about an hour and 45 minutes.
The total eclipse will first become visible in extreme northern Russia at 17:00 UTC, which is 1 p.m. Eastern time.
It will reach northeast Greenland by 1:30 p.m. ET and western Iceland by about 1:45 p.m. ET (totality will be at exactly 5:48 p.m. local time in Reykjavík).

After crossing the northern Atlantic for 45 minutes — when it will be best visible in the U.K., with London reaching its max of 91% at 2:13 p.m. ET (7:13 p.m. local time) — totality will reach northern Spain at about 2:30 p.m. ET (exactly 8:32 p.m. local time in Valencia).
The whole path will be over by 2:45 p.m. ET.

For those in North America seeing a partial eclipse, it will be most full in Toronto at 1:40 p.m. and New York City at 1:54 p.m. local time. In Fairbanks, you will need to get up early to see its fullest point at 8:27 a.m. local time.
How do I watch the eclipse in person?
If you are lucky enough to be in one of the locations where the solar eclipse reaches totality, it will last for about two minutes.
You will need to wear solar eclipse glasses to safely view the sun during the event to protect your retinas from damage. You can take your glasses off for that two minutes when it's at totality.
If you're outside the path of totality but lucky enough to at least get a partial eclipse, you'll have to leave those glasses on the whole time to avoid eye damage.
When is the next total solar eclipse in the U.S.?
If hearing about the total solar eclipse in Europe gets you excited for the next one in the U.S., you have some time to wait.
The next total solar eclipse over the U.S. will be in 2044, but that one will only be visible in three states: Montana, North Dakota and South Dakota.

The next year, there will be another opportunity visible in many states as it moves from coast to coast. The eclipse will start in Northern California and move in an arc towards the east, ending in Florida, similar to one in 2017. There will be numerous U.S. cities where eclipse watchers can view the total eclipse, including Reno, Nevada; Colorado Springs; Tulsa, Oklahoma; Little Rock, Arkansas; Jackson, Mississippi; and Orlando, Florida.
There will be another in 2052 that crosses the Southeast, including Florida, Georgia and South Carolina.
To see a total eclipse in the northeastern U.S., you'll have to wait all the way until May 1, 2079.
How to watch coverage of the 2026 total solar eclipse

Most major cities in Europe will see at least 90% totality, including Madrid, London and Paris. title: Trump secretly switched to different plane in Turkey amid Iran threat
summary: Ahead of a flight from Turkey, President Trump secretly left Air Force One and was moved to another plane with the help of a catering truck, according to a source, as the U.S. grappled with a threat from Iran.
story: Shortly before Air Force One took off from Turkey at the end of last month's NATO summit, President Trump secretly slipped away from the presidential jet and was whisked to another plane with the help of an airport catering truck, according to a U.S. official with direct knowledge of the matter.

The ruse was employed because the U.S. had learned of a threat from Iran and its allied proxies. U.S. intelligence had detected a credible plot to fire a missile at the plane Mr. Trump was on as he left the Turkish capital of Ankara, CBS News reported exclusively.
The president had expressed awareness of the risks posed by the U.S.-Iran war, calling himself Iran's "number one target" during the NATO summit.
The Washington Post was first to report on the secret plane-switching.

Multiple Trump administration officials expressed frustration Monday night that highly classified tactics and procedures leaked into the public eye, potentially limiting future protective operations for U.S. presidents.

Hours before the move, on July 8, Mr. Trump announced he would leave Ankara in the old Air Force One rather than a newer Qatari-donated jet that he had taken to the NATO summit. The president said he was switching planes "for old time's sake," and U.S. forces stationed at a U.K. refueling stop would be able to check out the new plane, but CBS News has reported that the Secret Service advised that he take the older plane for security reasons.

Video footage captured by the press showed the president walking up the stairs of the old Air Force One and disappearing into the plane, with a catering truck visible on the other side of the jet. Several minutes later, the truck pulled away and drove off to another U.S. government plane, which the Post reported was an Air Force C-32A.

Mr. Trump then flew from Ankara to a refueling stop in the United Kingdom on the separate plane while members of the press and the president's staff traveled the same route on Air Force One — and believed they were on board the same aircraft as the president.

While in Ankara, members of the press were told to keep the window shades in Air Force One's press cabin closed, reporters said at the time. Asked why the shades needed to be closed, Mr. Trump later told reporters they were "probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleazebags that we have to deal with."

In the United Kingdom, Mr. Trump switched to the newer Air Force One, which was donated by the government of Qatar last year and retrofitted by the U.S. Air Force to serve as the new presidential plane. Mr. Trump spoke to members of the press while they flew across the Atlantic toward Washington, D.C.
The Trump administration has never publicly disclosed that the press and some members of the president's staff were flying on a decoy plane.

Last month, the new Air Force One — which debuted in June — was sent off to be "maxed out" with additional upgrades, the president told reporters, after questions arose about the newer plane's security features.

Asked Monday about the decision to secretly switch planes in Turkey, White House communications director Steven Cheung didn't respond directly to the question, saying in a statement: "The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff. As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats."
The Air Force has also called the new presidential plane "safe, secure and equipped with the most advanced technologies necessary to meet the requirements of the presidential mission."

title: Perseid meteor shower reaches peak viewing on Wednesday night
summary: The Perseid meteor shower is the best viewing all year, according to NASA.
story: The Perseid meteor shower is set to provide a late-summer show in the skies over the United States.
The meteor shower, which NASA calls the best of the year, is set to peak on Aug. 12 and 13.

"With swift and bright meteors, Perseids frequently leave long 'wakes' of light and color behind them as they streak through Earth's atmosphere," according to NASA. "The Perseids are one of the most plentiful showers with about 50 to 100 meteors seen per hour."

For those who are trying to see the meteor shower on Wednesday night, the best time for viewing in the Northern Hemisphere is during the predawn hours on Aug. 13, but if you don't want to get up very early, you can still see them as early as 10 p.m. the night before.

Random meteors are visible in dark skies on any given night. Meteor showers tend to put on dazzling celestial shows and happen at predictable times every year when the Earth plows through trails of debris left behind by comets and, sometimes, asteroids. Those remnants collide with Earth's atmosphere at extremely high speeds, producing streaks of light known as shooting stars.

The Perseids are debris from comet 109P/Swift-Tuttle, an icy ball that orbits the sun every 133 years and isn't scheduled for a return visit until 2125. Observations of this meteor shower date back over 2,000 years.
The Perseids are a perennial favorite because they tend to produce brilliant fireballs. Summer temperatures also make this shower popular.
"We don't have to suffer through a cold winter night to get a good view of meteors," said astronomer Zach Vanderbosch with McDonald Observatory in Texas.
The moon will be in its new moon phase during the Perseids' peak, making viewing conditions even better.

"The moon is beautiful, but it's such a diva," said astronomer Aparna Venkatesan with the University of San Francisco. "New moon means we don't have moonlight flooding the sky, and you tend to see way more meteors as a result."
To spot the meteors, go outside after dark, away from clouds and city lights. Venkatesan plans to drive to the Sierra Nevada.
The best views will be between midnight and dawn when the constellation Perseus is high in the northern sky. The meteors will appear to radiate from that constellation.

Look up and give your eyes a half hour to adjust to the darkness. Vanderbosch recommends picking a patch of sky to focus on until a quick, bright streak passes by — even in your peripheral vision — and to avoid looking at your phone.
"There's just something magical about it," Vanderbosch said.

title: Congo Ebola death toll tops 2,000 in fastest spreading outbreak on record
summary: At least 2,000 people have died among the confirmed cases in Congo's Ebola outbreak that is the fastest-spreading on record, according to the latest government data.
story: Bunia, Congo — At least 2,000 people have died among the confirmed cases in Congo's Ebola outbreak that is the fastest-spreading on record, according to the latest government data, as health authorities struggle to get help quickly to remote localities due to rebel conflict, bad roads and work stoppages over payment issues.
Data published overnight into Tuesday showed the outbreak has recorded a total of 4,381 confirmed cases, including 2,011 deaths.

The grim toll comes nearly three months since the outbreak was declared on May 15. While it took about nine weeks for the outbreak to record 1,000 deaths, it's taken just around three weeks to record the additional 1,000 deaths, showing how fast the health crisis is moving beyond the control of responders.
It's already the second-largest outbreak in history, only behind the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak that recorded more than 28,000 cases including over 11,000 deaths.
The World Health Organization has declared the outbreak, which has also led to cases in neighboring Uganda, a public health emergency of international concern.

Aid workers say the outbreak continues to outpace the response that's been expanding across the five provinces affected. Many health workers have gone on strike to protest not being paid for their work since the outbreak was declared. And most new cases are recorded outside of contacts that are being monitored.

The Ebola outbreak is unlike most previous ones because the rare Bundibugyo virus responsible for it has no approved vaccines or treatments. Clinical trials for those have begun in Ituri, the epicenter of the outbreak.

The WHO said on Monday that the outbreak likely started in February, long before authorities detected it in one of Congo's most remote and vulnerable areas. WHO said some cases early on were wrongly attributed to malaria and typhoid, and that early testing was conducted for the more common type of Ebola.
The WHO regional director for Africa, Dr. Mohamed Yakub Janabi, told a news conference that officials are "chasing the virus, the virus is ahead of us."
The first Ebola virus to be identified was in 1976 near the Ebola River in what is now Congo. The current outbreak is the 17th — and largest — the Central African nation has faced.

title: Zelenskyy says Russia using North Korean missiles in Ukraine
summary: Russia and North Korea have been collaborating in the offensive against Ukraine since 2024.
story: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of using North Korean ballistic missiles in its attacks, as another night of bombardment killed at least nine civilians and injured dozens of others.

Zelenskyy said Russian forces used ballistic missiles supplied by North Korea in their attack on the southeastern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, where local officials said six people were killed and 19 wounded.
Three more people, including a 15-year-old boy, were killed by Russian drones and artillery in the central Dnipropetrovsk region, local authorities said.
Russia has received additional ballistic missiles from Pyongyang and is preparing to deploy more North Korean troops, Zelenskyy said late Monday.

Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un signed a strategic partnership agreement in 2024 that pledged mutual aid if either country faced aggression. Since then, various reports of Ukrainian troops skirmishing with North Korean counterparts have emerged.

The Ukrainian president warned that North Korea's missile capabilities are being improved by the collaboration with Russia. "The more North Korean strikes there are here in Ukraine, in Europe, the more their missiles and soldiers are used, the more they correct their shortcomings and blind spots, the greater the danger will later be for Japan, the Republic of Korea, the Philippines, and other countries in the region," Zelenskyy said on social media.

In December 2024, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff estimated that there had already been more than 1,000 North Korean troops in the war. In January 2025, Ukraine announced it had, for the first time, captured two wounded North Korean soldiers.

Ukraine says Russia is scaling up its production of ballistic missiles, aiming to exploit Kyiv's critical shortage of Patriot air defense interceptors that can stop them. Kyiv also claims Moscow is preparing an increase in recruitment for a new push on the front line that stretches 775 miles along eastern and southern Ukraine.

"Every step Russia takes — increasing ballistic missile production, bringing in North Korean equipment, preparing for mobilization — all of this shows that Moscow is preparing not for peace, but for escalation," Zelenskyy said on social media.

title: 7.4 earthquake strikes western Colombia, killing at least 111 people
summary: The 7.4 magnitude earthquake's epicenter was in San José del Palmar, about 250 miles west of Colombia's capital, Bogota, officials said.
story: A strong earthquake with a magnitude of 7.4 struck western Colombia on Monday, killing at least 111 people, injuring at least 87 and causing major damage across the region. It was the largest quake to hit the South American country on record.

The epicenter was in San José del Palmar, a community in the rural Chocó province about 250 miles west of Colombia's capital, Bogotá, the U.S. Geological Survey and its counterpart in Colombia reported. The quake hit at about 8:34 a.m. ET and was followed by a 5.0 magnitude aftershock less than an hour later, USGS reported.

"You are not alone," Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella said in a video message. "Colombia has a president who cares about the people and who will do everything in his power to help them in the most difficult moments."

Most of the deaths were reported in provinces neighboring Chocó, including at least 40 in the Risaralda region, where the hard-hit city of Pereira is located, and 27 in the Valle del Cauca region, where Colombia's third-biggest city, Cali, is located.

Chocó Gov. Nubia Carolina Córdoba-Curi said on social media that at least 12 people had died in her province. Four deaths were reported in the city of Manizales in the Caldas region. A 73-year-old man died in the Antioquia province, the governor said.

The earthquake prompted evacuations as far away as Bogotá. Witnesses reported feeling the shaking across the capital and all the way to the coast in Barranquilla, as well as in Ecuador to the south. About 10.5 million people experienced strong to very strong shaking, according to USGS.
"The quake was very, very strong," Valeria Polo, a 29-year-old content creator in Bogotá, told the Agence France-Presse news agency.

The quake left cities, including Cali, Manizales, Pereira and Quibdó, ravaged with a mix of residents and search teams picking through the rubble of collapsed buildings. More than 20 municipalities across the country had been hit and hundreds of buildings were damaged, officials said.
In Cali, a city of 2 million people, there were 30 collapsed structures, Mayor Alejandro Eder said on social media. Eder urged residents to remain calm and report any damage as soon as possible.
Jorge Moncayo, a 64-year-old taxi driver in Cali, said he saw plumes of dust shoot up across the city from his home.
"My entire house shook," he said. "I've never lived through such a powerful earthquake."
Pereira's mayor, Mauricio Salazar, told a local radio station that at least 18 people had died in the city and that many more were trapped under "a massive quantity of collapsed buildings."
At the airport in Pereira, videos showed pieces of the ceiling falling down on travelers taking shelter and screaming, and people running through rubble in a panic.

Manizales Mayor Jorge Eduardo Rojas said on social media that 17 buildings in the city had collapsed and 19 had partially collapsed. Images showed one of the towers of the city's neo-Gothic cathedral had collapsed and fallen on the nave.
Flights were suspended at multiple airports, including in Pereira, Manizales, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura, Colombia's aviation agency said.
In Armenia, several people have been evacuated from their homes over structural damage fears.
No structural damage was reported in Bogotá, Mayor Carlos F. Galán said.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a social media post on Monday that the Trump administration was closely monitoring the earthquake and "stands ready to support the people of Colombia."
South Florida organizations are among U.S.-based humanitarian groups mobilizing to send aid to Colombia.

"There's a lot of damage, and we are waiting for information as to what the needs are. The first is rescue and recovery," Fabio Andrade, the city of Weston's commissioner and a Colombian American, told CBS Miami.

Monday's earthquake was the strongest to hit Colombia since record-keeping started in the early 1920s. The country lies along the "Ring of Fire," the line of seismic faults encircling the Pacific Ocean where most of the world's earthquakes occur.
The area hardest-hit by the quake, Colombia's coffee region, was devastated by an earthquake in 1999 that killed more than 1,200 people.

The seismic activity in Colombia also follows two back-to-back 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude quakes that struck neighboring Venezuela in late June, which caused widespread damage and killed more than 5,000 people.

title: Ukrainian drone strikes deep inside Russia kill at least 13, authorities say
summary: The death toll is one of the highest among Russian civilians in recent months, as Ukraine seeks to disrupt Russia's oil supply.
story: At least 13 people were killed, including a child, and 78 others were injured in a Ukrainian drone attack in the Russian republic of Tatarstan, authorities in the region said. It was one of the highest civilian death tolls in the country in recent months.

The head of Tatarstan, Rustam Minnikhanov, said the city of Nizhnekamsk, which is roughly 750 miles east of the Ukrainian border, came under a "massive" drone attack targeting industrial and civilian facilities on Monday morning. Russian media reported that the attacks hit a major oil refinery.

Ukrainian officials confirmed their military had struck the oil facility "as part of efforts to reduce the Russian aggressor's military capabilities." Ukraine has targeted Russian oil facilities with long-range drones almost daily in recent months in an attempt to reduce Russian oil refining capacity to put further pressure on the country's fuel supply and economy.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says it is a campaign to try to force Russian President Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table and stop his more than four-year-old invasion.

"We do deliver entirely justified responses, and every Russian strike will be met with our response. Russia's war will be felt more and more at their own home – in Russia," Zelenskyy said late Sunday on social media. "The only reason this is still continuing is Russia's unwillingness to end this war."

Russia has also regularly battered Ukraine from the air using missiles, powerful glide bombs and drones, hitting civilian areas and causing thousands of civilian casualties, according to the United Nations.
The World Health Organization's European office said Monday that one of its warehouses in the central Dnipro region of Ukraine had been struck twice in less than 24 hours.

title: Italian businessman is mastermind behind journalist bomb attack, police say
summary: Valter Lavitola, a former journalist and import-export businessman who owns a restaurant in Rome, was close to former Italian premier Silvio Berlusconi.
story: A businessman who had ties to former Italian premier Silvio Berlusconi is the alleged mastermind behind an October bomb attack against one of the country's leading investigative journalists, police said on Monday.
Rome's Carabinieri police said they arrested Valter Lavitola for allegedly ordering the attack outside journalist Sigfrido Ranucci's house last year. The two men are said to be friends.

The blast in a residential neighborhood of Pomezia, about 12 miles south of Rome, destroyed two cars belonging to Ranucci, known for investigations into corruption and the mafia. Ranucci had just returned home at the time, and his daughter had walked by a half-hour before, his employer said at the time.
Video shot by Ranucci, who has been under police protection since 2021 because of his hard-hitting investigations, showed the mangled remains of the cars and the gate.

Lavitola is accused of instructing a second man, Tavares Gomes Clesio, to recruit four men to place the bomb in front of Ranucci's home, police said. The four men were arrested near Naples in June for carrying out the attack.
Police are still looking for Gomes.
According to police, Lavitola and Gomes took part in an "initial exploratory inspection" outside of Ranucci's home in September.
Lavitola thought the bombing would raise Ranucci's profile ahead of a possible career in politics, authorities wrote in the arrest warrant, according to local media.
Ranucci, the popular star of the weekly investigative show "Report" on state broadcaster Rai, is not accused of any wrongdoing and detectives believe he was unaware of Lavitola's plans.

Ranucci has taken on sensitive topics such as Italy's mafia and political corruption in past investigations, and has lived under police protection for years. He told the ANSA news agency the day after the attack that he had received "an endless list of threats."
The journalist, who once described Lavitola as a "true friend," was not injured in the attack.
Lavitola, a former journalist and import-export businessman who owns a restaurant in Rome, is well known in Italy, having been close to Berlusconi, who died in 2023.

In 2015, a lower court convicted the former prime minister of having bribed a senator, handing him a three-year sentence. The same sentence was given to Lavitola, whom prosecutors accused of having handed the cash to the lawmaker.

The explosion targeting Ranucci occurred on the eighth anniversary of the car bomb slaying of Maltese investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, who wrote extensively about suspected corruption in political and business circles.

story: Spokane, Washington — More than 40 large wildfires are burning in the West, fueled by severe drought, as over 100 blazes scorch parts of western Canada.
The Bug Fire near Reno, Nevada, has burned more than 15,000 acres, getting dangerously close to homes and forcing thousands of residents to evacuate over the weekend.
In Utah, two pilots were killed after their helicopter crashed on Friday while fighting the Widemouth 2 Fire, which has grown to more than 100,000 acres.

And in British Columbia, Canada, which borders Washington, the Bald Range Fire burned out of control, nearly doubling overnight as residents raced out. More than 20,000 people were ordered to evacuate the area of Summerland — 150 miles east of Vancouver — and officials say some residents had to be rescued.

"Aerial response teams were converted to emergency evacuation personnel," said Ravi Parmar, minister of forests of British Columbia. "Eighteen of our aircraft were used to rescue more than 50 individuals."
British Columbia declared a province-wide state of emergency Saturday as more than 100 wildfires burned across the province amid windy weather and prolonged drought.
Last week, fires near Spokane, Washington, showed how quickly conditions can escalate. Blazes there destroyed nearly 1,000 structures.
Some evacuations in Spokane eased Sunday, but the hardest-hit neighborhoods remain closed while crews check for hot spots.
Spokane County Sheriff John Nowels said authorities were doing everything they could to get people back in their homes "as soon and as safe as possible."
Officials have not said exactly when families in the hardest-hit areas can go home. Crews are still monitoring for hot spots and removing hazardous materials.

title: London police seize record $10 million in supercars in one weekend
summary: One of the vehicles impounded was a Ferrari Monza SP2, which can sell for as much as $5 million at auction.
story: London police said Monday they had seized a record $10 million worth of supercars between Friday and Sunday in an operation aimed at curbing antisocial driving.

Officers from London's Metropolitan Police seized a total of 90 vehicles across popular affluent London neighborhoods such as Hyde Park, Kensington and Chelsea, marking the highest value and number of cars impounded since they launched an operation to crack down on antisocial driving five years ago.
Authorities in England consider antisocial driving to include causing unnecessary noise pollution, street racing and cruising in a convoy, among other types of public nuisance.

In the summer months, it is common for owners of expensive and exotic cars, domestic or otherwise, to descend on some of central London's affluent and popular neighborhoods, often meeting up in groups. It's not uncommon for some drivers to be heard unnecessarily revving their engines, prompting complaints from locals.

"The disruption caused by these reckless drivers and boy racers is often worse during the summer months and, as well as putting people at risk, causes significant nuisance for residents and businesses," Caroline Sargent, a lawmaker at Westminster City Council, said.
This year, police have been given the power to seize vehicles involved in antisocial behavior rather than giving motorists a warning, the Met Police said in a statement.

One of the vehicles seized included a Ferrari Monza SP2, which was one of only 499 made and can be auctioned for nearly $5 million. The police said the car had only been in the U.K. for a day and had no insurance. The driver was also on a provisional driving license, which can only be used for learning how to drive.

Special Chief Inspector Geoff Tatman, who led the operation, said, "We regularly hear from local people who are fed up with people driving cars dangerously in the area, or with modifications which make them a nuisance to those who live nearby.
"Through operations like this, we're arresting these drivers and seizing their cars so we can keep our roads safe."

title: Undersea power cable diverted after "Harry Potter" fans complain
summary: The CEO of Etchea Energy described being inundated with calls after inadvertently planning an underground cable beneath a memorial to the fictional "Harry Potter" character.
story: The construction of a multimillion-dollar electricity connection project between Ireland and the U.K. was slightly diverted after "Harry Potter" fans complained the infrastructure would disturb a memorial for Dobby, the fictional elf in the popular book series.

The CEO of Etchea Energy, Simon Ludlam, told the "Energy Revolution" podcast his company had initially planned to build part of the connection through Freshwater West, a beach on the coast of Wales, and had received permission from the relevant authorities.

Ludlam said that he was unaware of the meaning of the memorial when he gave an interview to BBC Wales and explained that the high-voltage subsea and underground power cable system would make landfall, underground below the beach, through dunes and into the electrical grid.
After the segment aired on TV, the CEO said the company received "hundreds of calls" from "Harry Potter" fans, prompting his colleagues to urge him to respond to the backlash.
"Apparently we're going to go straight through Dobby's grave," Ludlam recalls being told. "I said, 'Dobby? Who's Dobby?'" he told the podcast host.
"I said, 'He's a fictitious character in a fictitious book, the whole thing is fictitious, what are you talking about?'"

After being told the complaints were "very, very serious," Ludlam said the firm went back to the planners and discussed how to divert the cable in order to avoid Dobby's memorial, and instead ended up going "quite close" to Bronze Age remains.
"We avoided Dobby's grave; a lot of people were very happy about that, the project's now going, and Dobby's happy," Ludlam remarked.
Discussing the need to be flexible when planning major infrastructure projects, the CEO added that "sometimes, a 10-year-old girl is right."

In 2022, environmental officials from the National Trust Cymru, the agency which manages the beach, asked fans to stop bringing socks and other items because they said it would be harmful to local wildlife.

title: Wildfires in western Canada force more than 20,000 people to evacuate
summary: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said an 80-year-old woman died while trying to escape a wildfire that forced evacuations in the Okanagan Lake region.
story: A fast-moving wildfire in British Columbia has killed at least one person, destroyed homes and forced more than 20,000 people to flee communities along Okanagan Lake in western Canada, with dozens rescued by aircraft.

Premier David Eby announced a state of emergency Saturday as more than 100 wildfires burned across the province, nearly half of them out of control in hot, windy weather and prolonged drought. Thousands fled on jammed roads as officials warned that "explosive" conditions could threaten more communities.

Summerland, home to about 12,000 people, was ordered evacuated overnight, along with about 8,000 people in and around nearby Peachland. Eby's office confirmed "significant structure loss" but said officials could not yet assess the damage because the area remained an active fire zone.

At an evacuation center in Penticton, Summerland resident Anette Boulet said the approaching fire "looked like doomsday." She fled before dawn with her family and five dogs, unsure whether her home was still standing.

The speed of the fire forced even emergency officials to flee. Erick Thompson, an emergency official with the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen, said he had to abandon the emergency operations center and evacuate his family.
"I had to leave the EOC to come and get my family to leave this area. We're heading south," he said in a video posted early Saturday from his vehicle as traffic backed up around him.

Some residents were trapped as the fire advanced, Eby said, while search-and-rescue crews continued looking for others who may have been caught. British Columbia Forests Minister Ravi Parmar said 18 firefighting aircraft rescued more than 50 people.
"People have lost their homes. And many people have been displaced," Eby said.
The Bald Range wildfire, first reported Friday evening, raced roughly 9 miles toward Okanagan Lake within hours. By Sunday, the flames had scorched more than 53 square miles.
Anette Boulet was among residents who fled Summerland. As she and her family left around 4:30 a.m. Saturday, their home was shrouded in smoke.
"You couldn't see barely. It was, it was just dark, and the ridge, the ridge of fire just coming towards you," said Boulet, who evacuated to a center in Penticton.
"There's no words to express it," she said. "The fear."
Later Sunday, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police said an 80-year-old woman died while trying to escape the wildfire that forced evacuations in the Okanagan Lake region.

Eleanor Olszewski, Canada's minister of emergency management and community resilience, said Sunday on social media that she'd approved a request for federal assistance from British Columbia to provide shelter and accommodations for those forced to flee.

A British Columbia Wildfire Service perimeter map showed the fire had burned through areas containing numerous homes north of Summerland and reached Okanagan Lake. Videos posted on social media appeared to show homes burning as residents fled along roads with flames on both sides.
Eby called the sudden growth "a remarkable escalation in fire activity" and said the blaze became so intense that it generated its own weather system and lightning.
Cliff Chapman, the British Columbia Wildfire Service's director of operations, called conditions "explosive" and warned that other communities could face similarly fast-moving fires.

British Columbia Emergency Management Minister Kelly Greene said the state of emergency gives the province additional powers, including the ability to restrict travel and secure accommodations for evacuees that might otherwise be unavailable.
Highway 97, a major route through the region, was closed between Peachland and Penticton as roads filled with evacuees.

Canada has endured increasingly destructive wildfire seasons in recent years, forcing mass evacuations and repeatedly sending smoke across large parts of Canada and the United States. President Trump threatened Canada with additional tariffs in July after wildfires sent smoke into the New York City, Chicago, Detroit and Washington, D.C. areas, leading to severe air quality issues.
British Columbia experiences 1,600 wildfires per year, on average, according to the BC Wildfire Service.

title: Suspected Irish crime boss extradited from Dubai
summary: Daniel Kinahan, 49, faces charges of directing an organized crime group.
story: The alleged leader of an Irish organized crime gang has been extradited to Ireland from Dubai to face charges that he ran an international drug smuggling and money laundering empire with tentacles that stretched to Britain, Spain and the U.S.

Air Tracker data showed an Irish Air Corps plane from Dubai landing Sunday evening at a military airport on the outskirts of Dublin after courts in the United Arab Emirates refused to block his extradition.

The plane is believed to be carrying Daniel Kinahan, 49, who is expected to be taken directly to the Special Criminal Court in Dublin, where he will face charges of directing an organized crime group. He will then be held at the high-security Portlaoise Prison about 90 miles southwest of the capital, Irish broadcaster RTE reported.

Ireland's Special Criminal Court handles all organized crime and terrorism cases, as well as others where prosecutors believe the ordinary courts are inadequate to ensure the "effective administration of justice." Cases are heard by a panel of three judges without a jury.

Irish media report that a huge security operation was underway to ensure Kinahan faces justice. It will include armed police, members of the armed forces and the prison service — which recently acquired a bombproof escort van to transport organized crime suspects, terrorists and other high-risk prisoners, Irish broadcaster RTE reported.
The security precautions come amid allegations that the Kinahans are engaged in a bloody gang war with another Irish organized crime group.

"Since February 2016, the (Kinahan Organized Crime Group) has been involved in a gang war with another group in Ireland and Spain, resulting in numerous murders, including of two innocent bystanders," the U.S. Treasury Department said in 2022, when it sanctioned six members of the Kinahan gang and three businesses linked to it.

Irish police, with the help of authorities in Britain, Spain and the U.S., have been pursuing members of the Kinahan gang for the past decade. They allege that the gang smuggled tens of millions of dollars' worth of illegal drugs, including cocaine and cannabis, as well as guns into Europe, then used a network of apparently legitimate enterprises to launder the profits.

Daniel Kinahan is believed to have run the day-to-day operations of the gang from his base in Dubai, the U.S. Treasury said. That includes buying "large quantities of cocaine" from South America, organizing its distribution in Ireland and attempting to smuggle drugs into the U.K., the agency said.

Kinahan has also instructed gang members to deliver money to a number of people in prison, including one who was convicted of attempting to murder someone on behalf of the organization, the U.S. Treasury said.

In March of 2022, the head of the Kinahan organization in Britain, Thomas "Bomber" Kavanagh, was sentenced to 21 years in prison after he was convicted of orchestrating drug shipments into the U.K. Two other men were sentenced to 20 years and 19 1/2 years for their part in the crimes.

In the course of their investigation, police found 15 kilograms of cocaine and 220 kilograms of cannabis inside asphalt removal equipment fitted with a tracking device at the port of Dover on the English Channel, Britain's National Crime Agency said when Kavanagh was sentenced.

Kavanagh lived in a mansion equipped with bulletproof glass and reinforced doors in Tamworth, northeast of Birmingham. When police raided the property in 2019, they seized numerous weapons and 35,000 pounds of cash in various currencies, including Emirati dirhams and euros, as well as British pounds, the crime agency said.
In September of 2022, Spanish police arrested an Irishman suspected of laundering money for the Kinahan organization after raiding a property in Malaga on the Costa del Sol.

The organization was suspected of registering companies in Britain, Spain and Gibraltar, then creating a brand of vodka promoted in bars and nightclubs along the Costa del Sol to disguise the source of its earnings, according to the British crime agency, which assisted in the investigation.
"The Kinahan organized crime network transcends national boundaries, which is why international law enforcement operations like this are necessary," the agency said at the time.

title: Netanyahu rejects Gaza peace plan, vows no military withdrawal until Hamas disarms
summary: President Trump hailed the peace plan​ as a "historic agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all other groups in Gaza."
story: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday rejected a U.S.-backed Gaza peace plan and vowed there would be no military withdrawal until Hamas is "genuinely" disarmed.

Last month, President Trump hailed the peace plan as a "historic agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all other groups in Gaza." He said it was negotiated by his international "Board of Peace" and called it a "monumental step toward lasting peace and security."
On Sunday, after more than a week of gradually escalating criticism of the plan, Netanyahu explicitly opposed it as he faced pushback from his right-wing base ahead of elections.

"Israel rejects the 15-point document," he said in a cabinet meeting, adding that the military "will not make any withdrawal until Hamas is truly disarmed and will continue to thwart threats against our forces and citizens."

Under the plan, Israeli forces would withdraw from parts of Gaza as "disarmament is completed," Mr. Trump said in a Truth Social post on July 30, with an International Stabilization Force and a new Palestinian police force responsible for security.

"This agreement is a critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government that will work closely with the Board of Peace to help the Palestinian people," the president wrote. "At the same time, Israel will have the security it deserves, with Gaza no longer used as a base for terror attacks."
Netanyahu, who has faced calls from his far-right allies to hold a new cabinet vote and end the Gaza plan, said on Sunday that Israel is speaking with the U.S. about its objections.

"They have ideas, some of which are acceptable to us and some of which are unacceptable to us, and we know how to stand up to these things," he said. "We have proven this in the past and we are proving it today. In addition, the IDF will continue to thwart threats against our forces and against our citizens."
Netanyahu said Hamas must give up all of its weapons, a goal that Board of Peace members say is not realistically achievable.
"We are talking about real disarmament, not fictitious disarmament," Netanyahu said.
In response to Netanyahu's remarks, Hamas said Sunday that it remains committed to the roadmap reached by the mediators and the Board of Peace.

"Our acceptance of the roadmap, despite all the challenges, reflected a sense of national responsibility upheld by the resistance factions, foremost among them Hamas, in consideration of the interests of the Palestinian people," said Bassem Naim, a member of the Hamas political bureau, adding that it expects mediators and the U.S. to pressure Netanyahu.

The negotiations stem from a 20-point peace proposal that Mr. Trump offered last fall to end the war between Israel and Hamas. The conflict broke out with Hamas' terrorist attack on southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023.

title: 'Blue Bloods' star Jennifer Esposito says she was locked in psych ward as health battle spiraled
summary: Jennifer Esposito reveals how celiac disease caused liver failure, a psychiatric ward stay and thoughts of suicide before doctors finally diagnosed her.
story: Donnie Wahlberg told Fox News Digital that he did everything he could to keep "Blue Bloods" on-air before pivoting to the spin-off series.
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Jennifer Esposito is opening up about the yearslong health battle that she says derailed her career, left her severely depressed and eventually landed her in a psychiatric ward before doctors diagnosed her with celiac disease.

During an appearance on Maria Menounos' "Heal Squad" podcast, Esposito, 53, recalled being a young actress in New York City when unexplained physical and mental health problems became so debilitating that she was forced to put her life on hold.
"I had a whole life beginning in the city, and I was a young actor and I had to stop everything," Esposito said.
MAYIM BIALIK DETAILS 'NIGHTMARE' AFTER ONE INJECTION OF GLP-1 DRUG LED TO WEEKS OF DEBILITATING SIDE EFFECTS
Jennifer Esposito detailed years of misdiagnoses before she was ultimately diagnosed with celiac disease. (WireImage)
The actress said she became "deeply depressed" and began having "thoughts of suicide" as doctors struggled to determine what was wrong.

"They brought me to a psychologist, like they had me on every medication," she recalled. "They wanted to give me shock treatment at one point because I wasn't responding. I'm very sensitive to medication. It was a really bad time. And my mother had people pray over me."
Esposito said she eventually began to suspect that her physical and mental health symptoms could be connected to nutrition.
"I realized that there was a major connection with what I was eating and my vitamins and then my body," she said.
DAMON WAYANS REVEALS THE SCARY SYMPTOM THAT LED TO HIS TYPE 2 DIABETES DIAGNOSIS
Her health began to "collapse" while she was working on the ABC comedy "Samantha Who?," which aired from 2007 to 2009, according to the actress.
Esposito recalled experiencing alarming physical symptoms, including losing her hair and fingernails.
The 53-year-old actress said the symptoms took a toll on her physically and mentally. (JC Olivera/Getty Images)
"I had hair falling out, nails falling off," she said.
Then, she said, a tooth fell out while she was filming a scene.
CARLY SIMON REVEALS THE COMMON CONDITION THAT MASKED HER PARKINSON'S DIAGNOSIS
"A tooth fell out of my mouth, like literally in the middle of a scene," Esposito recalled. "I was mortified but also had been so ill that I just — I went hysterical. Like, somebody has to help me."

Esposito said she was misdiagnosed several times, with doctors considering conditions including multiple sclerosis and irritable bowel syndrome. She said a therapist suggested stress was behind her symptoms.
"Talk about gaslighting," she said.

"We don't ever treat the actual underlying issue. We treat symptoms in this country, in America," Esposito continued. "I went for years on that, and I tried everything myself. I went to holistic healers. I went to get my aura cleansed. I was vegan."
Desperate for answers, Esposito said she began attending a non-denominational church in an effort to "feel recharged."
On one drive there, she recalled reaching a breaking point.
Esposito said she was losing her hair and nails were falling off due to her nutrition issues. (Getty Images)

"I remember saying to myself, because I was so depressed of being so sick all the time and fighting panic disorders … ‘If you don't get a diagnosis, you have to accept the fact that you're crazy, and you've created this, and you're going to let it go because I can't keep doing this.’"
Moments later, she said, a large piece of wood flew from a truck in front of her and smashed through her windshield.
RANDY TRAVIS' HEALTH CRISIS BEGAN WITH 'CONGESTION' AND ENDED IN A FIVE-MONTH HOSPITAL STAY
"I'm sitting with glass all over me," Esposito said. After managing to pull to the side of the road, she took the frightening accident as a sign to continue looking for answers.
Two days later, Esposito said, a doctor called with her diagnosis: celiac disease.
"I’m not sure how you’re alive," Esposito recalled the doctor telling her.
According to Esposito, her case was so severe that her liver was failing.
The "Blue Bloods" star recalls being taken to a psych ward amid her misdiagnoses period. (Getty Images)
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Celiac disease is an autoimmune condition in which consuming gluten — a protein found in wheat, barley and rye — triggers an immune response that damages the small intestine. That damage can interfere with the body's ability to absorb nutrients and can cause symptoms extending well beyond the digestive system, including fatigue, anemia, neurological problems and elevated liver enzymes. A strict, lifelong gluten-free diet is the primary treatment and can allow the intestine to heal, according to the Mayo Clinic.
After receiving her diagnosis, Esposito immediately eliminated gluten from her diet, but said her body was in such poor condition that her recovery was grueling.

She recalled being severely deficient in vitamin D and developing welts when exposed to sunlight. Her nervous system was also so overwhelmed, she said, that ordinary stimulation became difficult to tolerate.

"They had me on four Klonopin a day, and I was still a trembling mess," Esposito said. "I was literally sleeping in my kitchen because it was the only place that didn't have a window, because the light — the stimulus from the light — would make me tremble and shake."
'GAME OF THRONES' ACTRESS SAYS SHE JOINED A WELLNESS CULT THAT LED TO A PSYCHOTIC BREAK
"It was horrendous," she added.
About two months after her diagnosis, Esposito began seeing a medical expert who she said wanted to study her because of the severity of her case.
Esposito said she eventually took matters into her own hands. (Getty Images)
She underwent regular blood and urine testing, but during one appointment, Esposito said she was in such distress that she pleaded with the doctor to keep her in the hospital.
"Doctor, you got to keep me here because I'm jumping out of my skin. I'm going to jump out the window," she recalled saying.
Esposito said the remark was interpreted as a threat of self-harm.
Within half an hour, she said, she was taken to a psychiatric ward under the alias "Betty Franklin."
"I will say it was seven of the most excruciating hours of my entire life because I was yet again pleading for my sanity," she said.
Esposito said her father was with her and recalled fearing that she would not get out if he left.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
"If you leave me here, I'm dying because I'm going to fight these people," she recalled thinking.
The actress said the experience became even more frightening when a doctor asked her father for permission to restrain her if she got "out of hand."
Esposito hopes her story can help others.  (FilmMagic)
Esposito forced herself to remain calm. "I thought, if I ever get out of here, I have to do something," she said.
After returning home, Esposito said she took an increasingly active role in understanding her condition and recovery.
"If you heal your gut, I promise you, not everything can go away," she said, adding that recovery "takes time."
Esposito, who said she now lives outside the United States, told Menounos that she no longer experiences panic attacks and has adopted a dramatically different pace of life.
"This is my life. I get to enjoy time," she said. "I sit down and eat lunch. I sit down and talk to people. There's no phones on the tables."
"There’s a grace given for enjoyment in life," Esposito continued. "I just think we've lost the plot with that. And no wonder why we're all sick."
Looking back on the ordeal, Esposito said she ultimately views her diagnosis as something that changed the trajectory of her life.
"Celiac disease saved my life. One hundred percent," she said.
Esposito said she believes the years of stress and living in "fight or flight" would eventually have taken an even greater toll had her illness not forced her to change course.
"I 100% would have been somewhere not good," she said.

Now, she said, she is "very, very, very clear and grateful" — including for the opportunity her experience has given her to help others.

title: ‘This Is Us’ star Chrissy Metz says she turned to GLP-1 drug after years of skepticism
summary: Chrissy Metz says she was "nervous and scared" to try a GLP-1 but her doctor recommended it, and she's now focused on longevity and overall health.
story: Ethan Suplee reflects on the ongoing responsibility that comes with becoming a public weight-loss success story and explains why consistent support from like-minded people keeps him on track.
Chrissy Metz is opening up about her decision to use a GLP-1 after years of skepticism about the popular weight-loss medications.

During an appearance on the "Today" show on Monday, the "This Is Us" star, 45, explained that she reconsidered the drugs as she entered perimenopause and thought more seriously about her health and her family's history with obesity.
"I was very skeptical about GLP-1s for years," she said. "I had a friend who was like, I don't know, he gave me a thesis, and I was like, 'OK, this might be helpful.'"
MAYIM BIALIK DETAILS 'NIGHTMARE' AFTER ONE INJECTION OF GLP-1 DRUG LED TO WEEKS OF DEBILITATING SIDE EFFECTS
Chrissy Metz said that she's started taking weight-loss medication. (Getty Images for A+E Global Media)
After witnessing her father experience complications with his own health, Metz thought, "Maybe I should try and get ahead of it."
"It was something that I thought would be good for me," she said.
Since taking the drug, Metz said she's noticed a difference in her energy level, as well as her "overall health."
Despite the previous skepticism, Metz said the most important thing for her is "longevity."

"Learning what it really was and how it affects everybody differently ... my doctor and my team were like, ‘Yeah, I think this would be beneficial for you,’" said Metz, who admitted she was "nervous" and "scared" to try it.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Metz admitted she was "nervous" to try taking a GLP-1. (Rodin Eckenroth)

"That's what's sort of beautiful, it's a whole lifestyle change," said Metz, who has also incorporated strength training and exercise into her regimen. "It's not just, 'Oh, I'm going to take a medication,' because it's not the easy way out. I think a lot of people think 'Oh, it's a magic wand,' and no, in fact, you have to be more diligent. It's good for me because I'm really putting myself first. It's something I've always wanted to do, but I have to really put into practice now."

"It's been a really wonderful journey," she added.
Her decision marks another chapter in a yearslong, highly public conversation surrounding Metz's weight and health.
Metz shot to fame playing Kate Pearson on NBC's "This Is Us," where struggles with weight and body image were a major part of the character's storyline.
Metz is best known for starring in "This Is Us." (Getty Images)
The actress said in a 2017 interview that "so many people are afraid of fat people," arguing that education and more open conversations about weight could help change those attitudes.
Metz has also spoken candidly about how her complicated relationship with food and weight began long before Hollywood.
In 2024, Metz recalled enduring what she described as mental, physical and emotional abuse from her stepfather while growing up.
"He would weigh me in the kitchen or threaten to lock the cupboards," Metz said during an appearance on "The Jamie Kern Lima Show."
Metz said she believes there is now greater awareness surrounding "food, food issues, food behavior" than there was when she was younger.

title: Former Disney star Jennifer Stone found a lifeline in the ER as fellow child actors spiraled
summary: Jennifer Stone reveals how working as an ER nurse has kept her grounded while balancing her return to the "Wizards of Waverly Place" franchise.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Jennifer Stone credited her work as an ER nurse with keeping her grounded after growing up in the heightened world of Disney Channel fame.
Stone’s two worlds collided when she found herself balancing the return of the "Wizards of Waverly Place" franchise with the realities of working in an emergency room.

"I was like trying to post, and my hospital has terrible Wi-Fi, so I was getting outside, trying to post and do my job with that, and then literally coming in and wiping a-- and I just was like, nothing keeps you more humble," she told Avery Woods during an appearance on the "Cheers" podcast. "Nothing keeps you more humble."
FORMER DISNEY STAR MAITLAND WARD SAYS YOUNG ACTORS WERE TREATED LIKE A 'PRODUCT' IN HOLLYWOOD FACTORY
Jennifer Stone says working as an ER nurse helped keep her grounded after Disney Channel fame. (Bruce Birmelin/Disney Channel via Getty Images)
The realities of Stone’s work in healthcare stood in stark contrast to the Hollywood bubble she experienced as a teenage Disney star.

"I mean, I joked that it was like Disney High, because it was," she explained. "I mean, everybody dated everybody. There were feuds, there were people mad at so-and-so, like it's just nonsense. It was our high school, right? So, all the high school stuff that would normally happen in that environment, but you have access to so many things you wouldn't normally have."
"You have money, you have all these things that at 16, in high school, you wouldn't have, so it's just a heightened version of high school, I think," Stone added.
Former "Wizards of Waverly Place" star Jennifer Stone found a new purpose on the front lines of healthcare. (Monica Schipper/Getty Images)
BROOKE SHIELDS REFLECTS ON BEING MADE A 'SEX SYMBOL' AT A YOUNG AGE AND HOW SHE TURNED THE PAGE ON FAME
Stone credited her parents with helping her avoid getting swept up in that world and maintaining a sense of normalcy.

"I would have probably been a mess," she said, referring to how things would have been without the support she had from mom and dad. "I mean, and it's sad, because I've been in this industry for so long that it's like I've seen people I used to audition with. I mean, last month, there was a girl that I used to see all the time, and we would hang out as kids, and she overdosed, you know what I mean? It's like there's so many sob stories with kid actors, and I got really lucky."

Stone said her parents, both computer science majors with no creative backgrounds, supported her acting ambitions because they recognized her passion for the craft. Their efforts to keep her grounded became particularly clear when a writers’ strike sent Stone home to Texas at 16 during the run of "Wizards of Waverly Place."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Jennifer Stone reflected on navigating Hollywood as a young Disney star before becoming a nurse. (Michael Tran/FilmMagic)

"I think it was second season or something, and I went and got my driver's license, and they were like, 'You need to get a job while you're here,' so I literally was an elf at one of those places that take pictures with Santa Claus and stuff," she recalled.

After "Wizards" ended, Stone said she still "needed to be humbled" and "taken down a few pegs." That perspective came in a far more serious way when she was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes at 20 and spent the following years in and out of hospitals.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Jennifer Stone says her experience as a Type 1 diabetes patient inspired her career in nursing. (Eric McCandless/Getty Images)
Her experience as a patient ultimately inspired Stone to pursue a nursing degree, while working through the COVID-19 pandemic further reshaped how she viewed the pressures of Hollywood.

"You do not sweat the small stuff," Stone explained. "The entertainment industry stuff, like I'll have my actor friends spin out about like, 'Oh, I didn't get a call back or this happened,' and I'm like, 'Doesn't f---ing matter. You're alive. You're getting to do what you love. You're alive. You're healthy, and you don't know how much time you have.'"
"It makes all this stuff so small and so much easier to digest because you've digested such bigger, harder things," she added. "You know, it's like exposure therapy."

title: Country star Tyler Hubbard says ‘The Chosen’ brought the Bible to life for his family
summary: Tyler Hubbard reveals how "The Chosen" sparked faith conversations with his kids and inspired his new single "All I Need Is You" for Season 6.
story: The country music star told Fox News Digital his children's reactions to "The Chosen" are "a testimony to how well the show was produced."
Country singer, Tyler Hubbard, is sharing why his most recent musical project is special for him.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 39-year-old musician spoke about the upcoming season of "The Chosen" and his corresponding album, as well as how the television show brought the Bible alive for his children and has started a "lot of conversations about Jesus and about all the different stories of his life."

"We talk through all these stories, we talk through all their questions, but then it doesn't go in one ear and out the other," he said. "It really kind of sticks. It could be two years down the road, we'll be reading a Bible story and they'll already know it. They're kind of teaching us or teaching their friends at that point."

He called the idea that the show helps his kids understand the Bible better "a testimony to how well the show is produced and how accurate" the stories it is telling are, saying it "is really special" to reference them in the Bible and then "reliving it with the kids."
Tyler rose to fame as one half of the country music duo, Florida Georgia Line. (Jason Kempin/Getty Images for Ford Motor Company)
MORGAN WALLEN AND ELLA LANGLEY HOLD THE TOP TWO ALBUM SPOTS IN AMERICA FOR FIRST HALF OF 2026

Hubbard shared that he and his family watch the show together as a tradition, noting that "it's really opened up our kids' eyes to the gospel and to Jesus and how he lived." When the chance to write a song for the show came up, Hubbard admits he "was excited about the opportunity."
WATCH: Tyler Hubbard says 'The Chosen' brings stories from the Bible alive for his kids

"It was just one of those things where a buddy of mine said, 'Hey, I've got the opportunity to letting us write a song for 'The Chosen' and if they like it, they might use it for something,' And I thought, 'Well, that'd be really cool.' Just something a little different for me," he said.

He explained that growing up he got into music by "leading worship in church," so "getting to write a faith-based song, a song that has some meat on the bone" and a deeper meaning, "and some heart and some truth behind it was really cool."
"So we had a great day and ended up that 'The Chosen' team really liked the song, and it turned into something special and something I'm proud of and excited to be a part of," he added.
Hubbard said he was excited about the opportunity to write a song for "The Chosen." (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for ACM)

The song, "All I Need Is You," is the first single from the new album inspired by the show and will be featured on the soundtrack of its upcoming sixth season. It dropped on Aug. 7. The unnamed album, from 5&2 Studios and Capitol Christian Music Group, is set to debut in the fall.
He also spoke with Fox News Digital about a unique injury he had while on a recent fishing trip with his family.
WATCH: Tyler Hubbard was 'excited' to write a song for season six of 'The Chosen'

"I was just fishing one morning, and I was on a river bank and I got caught in a bush with my back cast and I went to cast it and it just, I had a treble hook just stick me pretty hard right in the back of the head. I ended up, I couldn't get it out myself," he shared.
TYLER HUBBARD STAYS CALM AS WIFE PULLS FISH HOOK FROM HIS SCALP ON FAMILY CAMPING VACATION

After trying and failing to get it out himself, he "asked for some help from my wife," who then "spent about a half an hour dealing with it." During that time, his son took his phone and began filming the removal process.
The Florida Georgia Line singer shared that he got a fishhook stuck in his head while on a camping trip with his family. (Tyler Hubbard Instagram)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
He shared the video of his wife, Hayley, hard at work trying to get the fishhook unstuck on Instagram, captioning the post, "Breakfast had to wait…"

"We were way out, kind of in the middle of nowhere," he said about why they didn't go to the ER. "And we did have some people be like, you should probably go, maybe get that checked out, or maybe have someone else take it out. But I was pretty determined. I was like, 'Baby, you got to get this hook out of here, cause I don't want to leave this place and I don't want to mess up this day.' So anyway, she did a good job."
His Instagram followers shared they had also gone through similar experiences. (Tyler Hubbard Instagram)

In the background of the video, viewers can hear the couple's children asking various questions out of concern. One asks, "Is it bleeding mom?" with Tyler telling him, "Probably not bleeding a lot, but it might be a little."
They then asked him if it hurts a lot, with another telling him, "Dad, just don't think about it. Mom is just going to pull it right away."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

The comment section was full of people sharing similar experiences, with one saying: "Did that to my dad, first AND last time I ever fished….45 years ago 🤣 this made my stomach flip just like it did back then. You’re a trooper @tylerhubbard 🙌."
"I’m an urgent care nurse so we see a lot of this … we numb the area and then pull out with pliers 👏," another added.
Hubbard and his wife both shared footage of him with a hook stuck in his head on their social media. (Terry Wyatt/Getty Images)

Hayley also shared a video from their weekend camping trip on her Instagram, including clips of the family fishing, swimming, rafting and enjoying nature, writing in the caption, "next time we’ll try to avoid fish hooks in the head 🪝."

Lori A. Bashian is an entertainment news writer at Fox News Digital.

title: Prince William, Kate Middleton could seek 'gentleman's agreement' to protect Prince George at Eton: experts
summary: Royal experts say Prince George's dating life and school years at Eton College could test the limits of the British press agreement in the smartphone era.
story: Katie Nicholl, Vanity Fair royal correspondent and co-host of "The Royals Uncensored," says Prince George passed Eton's admissions process like other applicants before accepting his place at the prestigious school.
Prince William and Kate Middleton could use a "gentleman's agreement" when Prince George starts Eton College in the fall — and it could face the ultimate test in the smartphone era.

GB News reported that the Prince and Princess of Wales could forge an agreement with the British press to limit intrusions into the life of their eldest son. Royal author and former broadcaster Simon Vigar told the outlet it’s the same approach that protected the early days of their romance at the University of St. Andrews.
Fox News Digital reached out to Kensington Palace for comment.
PRINCE WILLIAM AND KATE MIDDLETON 'CAUTIOUS' ABOUT WHICH ROYAL APPEARANCES THEIR CHILDREN MAKE: SOURCE
Prince George of Wales is said to be excited that he'll be attending Eton College in the fall. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"Prince William and Princess Catherine are realistic enough to know that they cannot completely control the environment around Prince George," Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube's "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital. "Most people have a camera in their pocket now, and one photograph can be online and around the world before the palace even knows it exists."

"What they can do is establish very clear boundaries with the British press," she said. "There is a huge difference between legitimate coverage of Prince George carrying out public engagements and somebody photographing a teenager going about his public life at school. The palace cannot police every teenager with an iPhone, but the press can make a conscious decision not to create a market for those intrusive photographs."

Catherine, Princess of Wales, Prince William, Prince of Wales, and Prince George attended the 2026 Easter Matins Service at St. George's Chapel in Windsor, England, on April 5, 2026. (Mark Cuthbert/UK Press/Getty Images)
In June, Kensington Palace announced that George, who turned 13 on July 22, would attend the prestigious boarding school where his father and uncle, Prince Harry, were educated.
WATCH: PRINCE GEORGE EARNED ETON COLLEGE SPOT WITH NO SPECIAL TREATMENT: EXPERT

Eton College, founded in 1440 by King Henry VI, has educated generations of leaders, including 20 British prime ministers. George, who is second in line to the throne, will likely meet many of his future peers there.
British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital that the "new age" of smartphones and social media is one of the many reasons Eton College is chosen "among the elites."

Students from Eton College in the Mound Stand react to Harrow students during a cricket match between Eton and Harrow at Lord's Cricket Ground in London, England, on May 10, 2024. (Philip Brown/Getty Images)

"Many classmates are from extremely wealthy and well-connected families," she said. "Within this circle are unwritten rules of conduct. Throwing a pupil to the media risks being ostracized from the inner circles."
A view of Eton College founded by King Henry VI. (Archive Photos/Getty Images)
Eton College is known for fiercely protecting its students from prying eyes, creating a world within its walls where they can simply be pupils.
"For Prince George and every high-profile teenager, everything could become international news within minutes," royal broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital.
Boys make their way to classes at Eton College, date unknown. (Christopher Furlong/Getty Images)

"We're in a better place," she said. "Years ago, after Princess Diana's death, I believe Prince William and Prince Harry forced positive change. The old paparazzi harassment was replaced with something somewhat controlled and truce-like."

When William and Harry were in school, an informal agreement was reached between the palace and the British press: As long as the brothers were pursuing their studies, their privacy was to be respected, Vanity Fair reported.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Prince William signs in on his first day at Eton College on Sept. 6, 1995. (Anwar Hussein/WireImage)
According to the outlet, this media truce allowed William and Kate to quietly build their relationship outside the public eye when they were students.
Prince William stands at Eton College in Eton, United Kingdom, wearing a waistcoat as a member of the elite prefect society called "Pop." (Tim Graham/Photo Library via Getty Images)

William and Kate met in 2001 at the University of St. Andrews in Scotland. They were close friends before they began dating more than a year later. Their romance remained a secret for nearly two years before becoming public. That level of discretion, Vanity Fair reported, was made possible, in part, by the informal agreement with the press.
The couple married in 2011.
Kate Middleton is seen waving to members of the public during a visit to the University of St. Andrews in Scotland, on Feb. 25, 2011. (CARL DE SOUZA/AFP via Getty Images)

Vigar told GB News that William and Kate want to offer the same level of privacy to their three children. Their children's first romantic relationships as they grow older "are already the subject of careful consideration," according to Vanity Fair. If the press respects George's privacy while he's in school, it could set a precedent for his siblings, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, to enjoy the same discretion.

"The 'gentleman's agreement' is more than necessary now," said Chard. "Prince William knows firsthand what privacy during school gave him. This handshake is perceived as a little fragile now and not necessary due to traditional paparazzi. Friends at school with their smartphones can become instant paparazzi."
A young Prince Harry is seen here at Eton College. (Tim Graham/Getty Images)

"George will have mentors, both family and at school, to guide him through pitfalls. No one wants him to feel burdened at 13. He should have space to grow, to be with friends, to be pain-free at Eton."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The Prince and Princess of Wales, seen here on the Isle of Mull, western Scotland, on April 30, 2025, have agreed that their eldest, Prince George, will attend Eton College. (Oli Scarff/AFP via Getty Images)
The Prince and Princess of Wales are also navigating what it's like to raise a teenager.
During the Commonwealth Games in Scotland, cycling champion Laura Kenny invited the couple to "come and give it a go" on a tandem bike, The Telegraph reported.
Princess Catherine and Prince George attend the men's singles final at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club in London, England, circa 2022. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)
When Welsh TV presenter Gethin Jones asked the royal children if they would like to see their parents "on a tandem in the velodrome," George quickly said, "No."
Prince George is seen here with his younger sister Princess Charlotte in London on July 12, 2026. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)
"We embarrass you enough as it is," said William.
When the royal family received their own Welsh cycling outfits, William joked, "You know me, Lycra!"

Catherine, Princess of Wales, Prince William and Dame Laura Kenny watch track cycling during the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games at the Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome on Aug. 1, 2026, in Glasgow, Scotland. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
"I won't whip the shorts out," the prince promised.
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP

Prince George of Wales, wearing a hat and sunglasses, attends Day 14 of the Wimbledon Tennis Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club in London, on July 12, 2026. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)
Royal experts told Fox News Digital that the privacy challenge could become more complicated when George starts dating.

"George understands why people are interested in him," said Schofield. "A teenage girlfriend may find herself facing international attention simply because she sat next to him or was photographed leaving the same place. But Prince William will remember exactly what Catherine experienced. Her family, her friendships, her background and, eventually, almost every aspect of her life became subjects of enormous public interest."
Prince George of Wales attends Trooping the Colour on June 13, 2026, in London. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)

"I would expect William and Catherine to be fiercely protective when the day comes," said Schofield. "Especially while George and whoever he's dating are still minors. And I think the media has to exercise some common sense. A teenage romance involving Prince George is not automatically a royal courtship. Hopefully, we will all give him that space."

Prince William, Prince of Wales, Catherine, Princess of Wales, Princess Charlotte, Prince George and Prince Louis watch an RAF flypast from the balcony of Buckingham Palace after attending Trooping the Colour 2026 on June 13, 2026, in London. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital it's also likely William will remind his eldest son not to cause "mischief" while at Eton.
"George has been very family friendly, so I don't envision major changes in the dynamics," said Turner. "He must remember William knows every trick in the book."

Prince George of Wales and King Charles III watch an RAF flypast from the balcony of Buckingham Palace following the coronation of King Charles III and Queen Camilla at Westminster Abbey on May 6, 2023, in London. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"Eton was also picked due to its proximity to their home at Windsor," Fordwich pointed out. "Prince William credits his afternoon teas with his beloved grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, on Sundays. It was just a short walk from Eton. George will likely stay close to both his parents and spend time with them."
PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON FINALLY FEEL FREE TO SHOW AFFECTION IN PUBLIC: EXPERTS

Prince George of Wales watches an RAF flypast from the balcony of Buckingham Palace after the coronation of King Charles III and Queen Camilla at Westminster Abbey in London, circa 2023. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
Schofield told Fox News Digital that the Prince and Princess of Wales are determined to let George enjoy his school years and make new friends in private, without the added pressures of royal life.

"Teenagers naturally want independence," said Schofield. "Prince George is going to want to make his own decisions and develop interests that have nothing to do with becoming king. At the same time, public curiosity about him is only going to increase.

Prince George of Wales and Prince Louis of Wales stand during Trooping the Colour on June 13, 2026, in London, England. Trooping the Colour is a ceremonial parade celebrating the official birthday of the British monarch. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)

"These years could be enormously important in shaping the king he eventually becomes. William and Catherine had introduced royal life gradually rather than overwhelming him with it. We've seen George at family engagements, but he has still been allowed to be a schoolboy first."

Prince George and Prince William are seen at the UEFA Champions League quarterfinal match between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa at Parc des Princes in Paris on April 9, 2025. (Pierre Suu/Getty Images)

"The goal shouldn't be to manufacture the perfect future king at 13," she continued. "It should be to produce a confident, grounded adult who understands the institution but has also experienced enough of ordinary life to understand the people he will one day serve. Giving Prince George a genuine adolescence could ultimately be one of the best preparations for kingship William and Catherine can give him."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Suspect arrested at Kim Kardashian's mansion after stolen vehicle, break-in reported in Hidden Hills
summary: A suspect was arrested after a vehicle was stolen from Kim Kardashian's Hidden Hills mansion, which is currently under renovation and unoccupied.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
