title: Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs chooses former Republican as running mate in re-election bid
summary: Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs has chosen a former Republican as her running mate for her re-election bid this November.
story: Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs has chosen a former Republican as her running mate for her re-election bid this November.
On Tuesday, Hobbs named John Giles, who served as a GOP mayor of Mesa, Arizona, from 2014 to 2025, as her pick for lieutenant governor.
In a joint video announcement with Giles, Hobbs said she has fought for Arizonans as governor by cutting taxes, securing the border and supporting public safety.

“Now, for the first time in our state’s history, we are electing a governor and lieutenant governor on the same ticket. And the first thing I looked for in a running mate was someone who shares that value of putting Arizonans ahead of partisan politics,” Hobbs said.
Giles said, “I was a lifelong Republican before becoming an independent because extremists shouldn’t stand in the way of getting things done.”
Giles changed his party affiliation to independent in May and voted in the Democratic primary last month, Hobbs’ communications director Michael Beyer confirmed to NBC News.
Voters will elect a lieutenant governor for the first time this fall after a ballot measure creating the position was approved in the 2022 election.
The New York Times was first to report on Hobbs’ plans.

Hobbs faces a competitive race against Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., who previously chaired the conservative House Freedom Caucus and has served in Congress since 2017. Biggs has selected former state lawmaker Sine Kerr as his running mate. Biggs won the Republican primary last month, beating fellow Rep. David Schweikert and businessmen Scott Neely and Ken Miceli.

While mayor of Mesa, Giles endorsed then-Vice President Kamala Harris for president in the 2024 election and spoke at the Democratic National Convention in Chicago that year about his disappointment with the Republican Party.

“I’m a lifelong Republican, so I feel a little out of place tonight. But I feel more at home here than in today’s Republican Party,” Giles said in his remarks. “The Grand Old Party has been kidnapped by extremists and devolved into a cult — the cult of Donald Trump.”

He added: “I have an urgent message for the majority of Americans who, like me, are in the political middle. John McCain’s Republican Party is gone, and we don’t owe a damn thing to what’s been left behind.”
The nonpartisan Cook Political Report rated the governor’s race as leaning Democratic in the battleground state, which President Donald Trump carried in 2016 and 2024 and Joe Biden won in 2020.

In 2022, Hobbs defeated Republican Kari Lake in the gubernatorial election by less than 1 percentage point. Before serving as governor, Hobbs was Arizona’s secretary of state. She also has been the minority leader in the state Senate and a member of the state House.
Hobbs recently formed a coalition of former and current Republican and independent leaders who support her re-election, which included Giles and more than 50 other business leaders and officials.

The Democratic incumbent has touted her record of working across the aisle, including signing more than 900 pieces of bipartisan legislation into law, according to her campaign. She has also highlighted her efforts to expand affordable housing and secure the border and her repeal of the state’s 1864 near-total abortion ban.
Biggs, meanwhile, has promoted his relationship with Trump and has run on a campaign touting his support for lowering taxes and border security.

title: Former Marine held in Russia for more than 4 years has been released
summary: Former U.S. Marine Robert Gilman released from jail in Russia
story: A former U.S. Marine who spent more than four years in a Russian prison and is believed to be seriously ill has been released and was on his way back to the United States on Tuesday.
President Donald Trump announced the release on Truth Social, saying Robert Gilman, 32, was freed after he discussed the case with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump said Gilman, a teacher, was released “very much on a Humanitarian Basis,” with no exchange of prisoners having taken place. He is expected to land at Andrews Air Force Base in Washington, D.C.
The president added in his post that he had spoken to Gilman “and he had one request — A GREAT cheeseburger when he lands. I will take care of that!”
The Russian government has not commented on the release.

About 50 days ago, Gilman was diagnosed with a “dissociative stupor — a condition where he is non-responsive and unable to interact or eat,” Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., said in a statement following the man’s release.

“He was essentially catatonic and also suffered a severe case of pneumonia,” added Markey, who has been campaigning for Gilman’s release. “We don’t yet know the full details of his current condition or the long-term impact on his recovery.”
Gilman’s sister Lexie Hudson thanked Trump in a statement issued by Global Reach, an advocacy group representing his family.
“There is no other reason that Robert is alive today other than that President Trump heard about the case and took action,” she said.
“I am looking forward to seeing Robert. I haven’t been able to speak with him once since this all began,” she added. “We will make sure that he gets the treatment and support that he needs.”
Russia releases former Marine after four years in prison

Before his release, Hudson said in a statement on Sunday that  she was worried that he would die if he wasn’t freed. “I’m more afraid for my brother than I have been since this horrible nightmare started,” she said in the statement issued by Global Reach.

Her comments on Sunday came around a month after Russia’s Kommersant newspaper reported that Gilman had been ​admitted to a hospital. Quoting his lawyer Irina Brazhnikova, the business daily reported that he was receiving treatment but it was too early to talk about a diagnosis.

Gilman, who served in the Marines from August 2019 until August 2020, had been detained in 2022. He was initially handed a 3 ½— year sentence for beating a police officer after being taken off a train for causing a disturbance.

While serving his sentence, in October 2024 Gilman was accused of attacking a prison inspector during a cell check, beating an investigator and assaulting a guard; he was sentenced to eight years and one month.
Last year, his sentence was extended again to 10 years after he was found guilty of assaulting prison guards.
Gilman’s American supporters contend he was ill when he was first arrested and also that he was provoked while in prison into actions that led to further charges.
According to Markey, Gilman was “subjected to physical torture, forced medication, and provocations by Russian authorities,” throughout his detention.
“There is no doubt that his treatment by Russian authorities is the reason Robert is in this precarious state today,” he added.
Gilman was one of at least 10 Americans known to be imprisoned in Russia.

title: The most dramatic meteor shower of the summer peaks the day of a solar eclipse
summary: The Perseids’ peak coincides with another highly anticipated celestial event: a total solar eclipse that will be visible in parts of Europe.
story: One of the year’s brightest and most popular meteor showers peaks this week, offering a chance to see shooting stars cross a particularly dark sky, thanks to the new moon.
The Perseid meteor shower has been underway since mid-July, but is expected to peak overnight from Wednesday to Thursday.
Because the moon’s illuminated side is currently facing the sun, with its night side facing Earth, bright moonlight won’t interfere with one of the most anticipated skywatching events of the summer.

The Perseids’ peak coincides fortuitously with what is perhaps the season’s most eagerly awaited celestial event: a total solar eclipse that will be visible from Spain, a small part of Portugal, Greenland, Iceland and northern Russia on Wednesday.
A total solar eclipse happens when the sun, moon and Earth align and the moon passes in front of the sun, fully obscuring its light.

In locations where the eclipse will occur around sunset, people may see Perseid meteors during totality, the minutes when the moon fully blocks the sun’s light, leaving a fiery ring and temporarily darkening the skies.

The Perseids are typically one of the most popular meteor showers of the year because of their timing during warm summer months in the Northern Hemisphere (typically from around mid-July to late August) and its high rate of shooting stars. Under ideal conditions — clear weather and dark skies — the Perseids can produce as many as 100 shooting stars per hour.
Though the highest rate comes during the shower’s peak, shooting stars should continue to be visible over the next two weeks.

The Perseid meteor shower occurs when Earth passes through a cloud of dust particles and debris left over from a comet known as 109P/Swift-Tuttle, which was discovered in 1862. The streaks of light are created as the debris hits the atmosphere. The Perseids are known to produce fireballs, which are extra bright meteors that leave behind glowing trails as they disintegrate.

To see the Perseids from the Northern Hemisphere, the best timing is in the early hours before dawn. People should choose an unobstructed location under the darkest possible skies, away from city lights and other forms of light pollution.
NASA recommends letting your eyes adjust to the darkness for 20 to 30 minutes, then to sit back, look up and patiently wait for the shooting stars.

For most places in the Southern Hemisphere, the meteor shower’s radiant — the point in the sky from which the shooting stars appear to originate — won’t rise above the horizon, making them difficult to see.
NASA plans to host a virtual watch party on YouTube beginning at 12 a.m. ET Thursday, with a stream of live views from sky cameras at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama.

title: Family of NYC fashion designer found dead on Montauk boat to file wrongful death lawsuit
summary: The family of a New York City fashion designer found dead on a boat in the Hamptons last year is preparing to file a wrongful death lawsuit against the man she was with when she died.
story: The family of a New York City fashion designer found dead on a boat in the Hamptons last year is preparing to file a wrongful death lawsuit against the man she was with when she died.
Martha Nolan-O’Slatarra, 33, was found dead on a boat owned by Christopher Durnan, 61, and docked at the Montauk Yacht Club in the ritzy region of New York’s Long Island on Aug. 5 of last year.

Her family filed a summons with notice against Durnan in Manhattan Supreme Court last week, accusing him of assault, gross negligence, and reckless and wanton conduct in connection with Nolan-O’Slatarra’s death. The family is seeking a sum of $50 million in damages. Durnan has not been charged with any crimes in connection with the death.

A lawyer for Nolan-O’Slatarra’s family, Michael Bowe of Brithem LLP, said in a statement to NBC News that the family has conducted their own investigation of Nolan-O’Slatarra’s death and “does not believe Martha died from intoxicants.”
He said that EMTs found “blood in her mouth, on her chest and head, on the floor, and possibly behind her head” and reported “the body was cold despite her allegedly having just lost consciousness.”

Durnan did not immediately return a request for comment. An attorney for Durnan, Robert Holdman, told New York Magazine last year that his client was “absolutely destroyed” over Nolan-O’Slatarra’s death.
“He watched his friend die in trauma,” the lawyer said.
The Suffolk County Medical Examiner has not publicly released a final cause and manner of death for Nolan-O’Slatarra. The examiner’s office did not immediately return a request for comment.

The Suffolk County Police Department issued a statement in the days following Nolan-O’Slatarra’s death saying that her autopsy “did not show evidence of violence and her final cause of death is pending further examination.”
The police department declined to comment on the discrepancy between their statement and the new allegations.
East Hampton Town Police responded to a 911 call from a man reporting a woman unconscious on a boat docked around midnight the day she was pronounced dead, according to last year’s statement.
She was pronounced dead on the boat by first responders after good samaritans attempted to perform CPR on her, police said.

Nolan-O’Slatarra was originally from Ireland and owned a swimwear company East x East. She said in a 2024 interview with the Irish Independent that she came to New York to follow her dreams as a businesswoman.

“I was the small town girl who needed to get out to achieve her big dreams,” she said. “I always knew I wanted to be successful, that I was money-driven, business-driven — and that fashion is a tough industry and it would be a slow road.”

title: Arkansas high school football player finds deadly snake was in his helmet while he practiced for an hour
summary: An Arkansas high school football player discovered a venomous snake in the helmet he was wearing during practicing for almost an hour last week.
story: An Arkansas high school football player discovered a venomous snake in the helmet he was wearing during practicing for almost an hour last week.
The two-foot-long snake had found its way under the padding of the helmet on Thursday, staying hidden until the student noticed an unusual movement in the head piece.

Maumelle High School Athletic Director Kirk Horton told NBC affiliate in Little Rock KARK that his athletic staff was stunned when one of their players brought in his helmet for inspection after warmups, finding a cottonmouth snake trapped inside.
“It really was just shock and disbelief,” Horton said. “I’ve got a better shot at winning the lottery than seeing this in my ten years.”

title: Judge finds Kennedy Center owes musician $250,000 in legal fees
summary: A federal judge in Washington, D.C., ordered the Kennedy Center to pay $250,000 in legal fees to musician Chuck Redd, whom the arts center sued for canceling a Christmas Eve concert after President Donald Trump’s name was added to the building’s facade.
story: A federal judge in Washington, D.C., ordered the Kennedy Center to pay $250,000 in legal fees to musician Chuck Redd, whom the arts center sued for canceling a Christmas Eve concert after President Donald Trump’s name was added to the building’s facade.
Superior Court Judge Tanya Jones Bosier dismissed the case in June, finding conditions of unlawful retaliation against Redd.

In an order Monday, Bosier said that she made a “good faith evaluation of records to exclude hours that are arguably duplicative, excessive, or unnecessary” and found that the Kennedy Center owes Redd $252,479.70 for the legal fees he has accrued, to be paid within the next 45 days.
A Kennedy Center spokesperson said the organization intends to appeal the decision.
Redd’s attorney, Lisa J. Banks, said in a statement that the “Trump-controlled Kennedy Center tried to silence opposition to its illegal name change by filing a meritless lawsuit” against her client.
She called the penalty “appropriate as no citizen should have to spend time and money fending off baseless and politically motivated lawsuits filed by the Trump Administration.”
Redd had been scheduled to host the center’s annual Christmas Eve Jazz Jam on Dec. 24, 2025, but backed out of the free show on Dec. 19 after Trump’s name was added to the facade.
The president’s name was removed from the center in June after a board member successfully argued that the addition of Trump’s name was illegal.

The Kennedy Center had accused Redd of violating its “morals clause” after he went public with the reason why he’d backed out, which the center described as a decision “to abuse the public forum provided to him by the Center in order to make a political statement, and to deprive the public of the concert he promised.”
The center said his cancellation “incurred damages from lost goodwill with the public, wasted marketing expenses, and sunk costs preparing for a concert that did not occur.”
The facility’s then-president, Richard Grenell, had initially threatened to sue Redd for $1 million. The Kennedy Center later offered to settle with the musician for $7,500.

Redd countered that the concert was free and that he canceled early enough for the center to find a replacement. He noted that he had not signed a contract to perform, arguing that the only reason he was targeted by the center was that he had spoken out on a matter of “public interest.”
The judge sided with Redd, noting that he was one of several artists who’d been scheduled to perform at a show that was ultimately canceled anyway.

The “Center did not lose any ticket sales as the concert was free, and the entire performance was canceled as a result of multiple artists canceling, so the Center did not incur costs for staff or other performers,” she wrote in her June decision, also noting that Redd — the only one to have spoken out about the name change — appeared to be the only one who was sued.

title: Why is the U.S. banning a ton of robot vacuums? Here’s what you should know
summary: The FCC banned foreign-made advanced robots, and robot vacuums fall under the new rules. Here’s what it means for the device you already own — and which models you can still buy.
story: Robots are having a moment with the federal government — and it’s not all positive. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) recently announced a ban on foreign-made advanced mobile robots, a category that covers a ton of different types of robots. And while you probably don’t have a walking, talking robot in your living room yet, you might have something else the ban touches: a robot vacuum.
That everyday cleaning gadget falls squarely into the category now facing new restrictions, and it has nothing to do with battery recalls or overheating parts. Here’s what you need to know.
Why are robot vacuums being banned?

Late last week, the FCC added advanced robotic devices and foreign-made power inverters to its Covered List, the government’s running roster of tech that’s considered too risky to trust. The list flags communications equipment and services the FCC says pose “an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States or the security and safety of United States persons.”

What that means in practice is that anything on the list can’t get FCC equipment authorization. And without that authorization, a product typically can’t be imported, marketed or sold in the United States.

So why robots? According to the FCC’s National Security Determination, it comes down to what these devices can see and record. Robots are often packed with high-tech sensors that are constantly gathering data about the spaces they move through.

The concern isn’t just what the sensors collect, though. It’s also how the devices connect. Because robots typically operate on networks, the FCC notes they’re vulnerable to the same risks as any connected device: getting hacked, having data stolen or even losing control of the device itself.
What is covered under the robot ban?
While the ban seems mostly aimed at humanoid and animal-like robots, the “advanced robotic devices” category casts a much wider net. If a device checks these boxes, it qualifies for the ban,:

It can move, navigate or avoid obstacles on its own.It operates remotely, either through human control or by responding to sensor data.The device (plus any docking station) weighs more than 4.4 pounds combined.It has a sensor that reads its surroundings, can connect to a network at 200 kbps or faster, or runs software — including AI or machine-learning models — that controls how it moves, senses its environment or receives remote commands.
It can move, navigate or avoid obstacles on its own.
It operates remotely, either through human control or by responding to sensor data.
The device (plus any docking station) weighs more than 4.4 pounds combined.

It has a sensor that reads its surroundings, can connect to a network at 200 kbps or faster, or runs software — including AI or machine-learning models — that controls how it moves, senses its environment or receives remote commands.

Sounds like your vacuum, right? That’s because it probably is. Most robot vacuums move around on their own, connect to your Wi-Fi, gather data about your home’s layout and many weigh in above that 4.4-pound threshold. Put it all together, and they check enough boxes to land on the list.

If your robot vacuum is already part of your cleaning routine, take a breath: It’s not going to stop working, and no one’s coming to confiscate it. The ban only applies to new foreign-produced advanced robotic devices — but since so many robot vacuums are made (or built with components made) outside the U.S., that covers the vast majority of what’s currently on the market. The key word there is new. For now, you can still buy any of the existing models that are already available at retailers.
Robot vacuums you can still shop

As mentioned, the existing inventory of robot vacuums in the United States are still up for grabs. With that in mind, I’ve rounded up robot vacuums that are still available to shop today — some are even on sale (at the time of publishing).
Eufy X10 Pro Omni

NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez tested this model as a first-time robot vacuum owner and says it took him just about 15 minutes to understand how everything worked. The robot vacuums and mops, while its base station empties debris, dumps dirty water, refills clean water, dries mop pads and recharges the battery on its own. It also offers advanced navigation, obstacle avoidance, room mapping, no-go zones and customizable routines through the Eufy app.
Lefant Robot Vacuum Cleaner

The Lefant M210 is a compact vacuum built for small spaces and homes with pets. At 11 inches in diameter and less than 3 inches tall, it easily cleans under beds, sofas and other low furniture. Instead of a traditional roller brush, it uses a suction port that pulls in pet hair and dirt without the tangling that roller brushes are prone to. It also offers six cleaning modes, infrared sensors to navigate around furniture and avoid falls, and app, Alexa or Google Assistant controls. When the battery runs low, it automatically returns to its charging dock, making it a low-maintenance option for everyday upkeep.
Roborock Q7 L5 Robot Vacuum

The Roborock Q7 L5 vacuums and mops your floors at the same time, using strong suction to pull dirt out of carpets and crevices while a laser mapping system helps it find the most efficient path around your home. It’s built with anti–tangle brushes meant to resist hair wrapping, so you don’t have to clean them out as often, and the mop pads can clean dried-on stains from floors. You can use the app to set cleaning schedules and pick which rooms the vac should avoid.
iRobot Roomba 105 Vac Robot Vacuum

The iRobot Roomba 105 Vac cleans your floors on its own, using much stronger suction than older Roomba models, plus a brush along the edges and a main brush pick up different kinds of dirt. It uses laser mapping to scan and remember the layout of your home, so it can clean more thoroughly instead of bumping around randomly. You can control it through an app, which lets you schedule cleanings, focus on specific rooms and skip others.

title: Trump took a secret flight out of Turkey in an elaborate plot to hide his location amid Iran war
summary: President Donald Trump was whisked out of Turkey last month on a military aircraft in an elaborate plot to keep his location secret amid security fears from the war with neighboring Iran, according to a U.S. official with knowledge of the plan.
story: President Donald Trump was whisked out of Turkey last month on a military aircraft in an elaborate plot to keep his location secret amid security fears from the war with neighboring Iran, according to a U.S. official with knowledge of the plan.

The Washington Post was first to report the details of the clandestine operation, which included using a catering truck to get the president on the C-32 that flew from Ankara to the Mildenhall air force base in the United Kingdom.

The U.S. official confirmed the accuracy of these details. Trump deplaned the C-32, again secretly, and reboarded the older Air Force One jet to emerge in public view of cameras to eventually walk across the tarmac to the newer Qatari-donated jet, which lacks certain security measures and will soon be further retrofitted.

When reached for comment Monday night, White House communications director Steven Cheung did not dispute the Post’s story, which cited material reviewed by the Post, a U.S. official familiar with the operation and another person with knowledge of the president’s travel.

“The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff,” he said. “As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats.”

He provided a similar statement in July when asked why Trump flew on an older Air Force One instead of the newer one gifted by Qatar between Ankara and Mildenhall, and noted at the time that “distraction and misdirection” are some of the tools at the government’s disposal. The most recent statement did not include that phrase.
In both statements, Cheung said: “The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff.”
The White House on Monday also shared a statement from the U.S. Air Force about the new Air Force One that Trump decided not to fly on as he left Turkey.
“The aircraft is safe, secure and equipped with the most advanced technologies necessary to meet the requirements of the presidential mission,” the Air Force said.
The Secret Service did not immediately respond to a request for comment Monday night.
Senate Democrats want a briefing on exactly what happened.

“The Senate should be immediately briefed on the Iranian threats against the President, the extraordinary measures taken to get him out of Turkey, any risks posed to U.S. personnel, and any threat to the homeland,” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said in a statement Tuesday, adding it was “unacceptable that Congress was kept in the dark” and learned about the mission through news reports.
Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., on Monday night called Trump’s undisclosed travels “downright scary.”

“There has to be a congressional briefing because it involves not just the safety of the president,” he said during an interview with CNN. “I want to know what precautions were taken to make sure that all of the passengers on that Air Force One, which was judged too dangerous for the president to fly on, what precautions were taken to keep the staff and reporters on that plane safe.”

Trump announced on the morning of July 8 that he would take the “former Air Force One” from Turkey to the U.K. “for old time’s sake.” He said the new Qatari-gifted plane would be taken separately to Mildenhall air base in Britain to give troops a chance to see the new jet.
That evening, Trump boarded the old Air Force One in Ankara in front of TV cameras.

As the events of the secret mission unfolded, journalists who usually travel with the president, already on board the old Air Force One, were instructed to lower their window shades, according to a press pool report from that day.

When speaking to reporters during the flight from Britain to the United States on the Qatari-gifted plane, Trump was asked why journalists had been instructed to close their blinds, a detail the reporter asking the question called “weird.”
“You’re probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleaze bags that we have to deal with,” Trump said.
Asked at the time if he was aware of a credible threat against him from Iran, Trump said he has “a threat all the time.”
“I’m No. 1 on their list, before you. But if I go, you go, right?” Trump told reporters. “Perhaps someday you want to change professions.”
He also denied that there were security issues with the new Air Force One plane that could have prompted him to switch aircraft in Turkey.
The U.S. government has undertaken decoy missions to protect U.S. presidents before, but their whereabouts were later revealed to the public.

In the hours after the terrorist attacks of Sept. 11, 2001, the White House told reporters that President George W. Bush was taken to an “undisclosed location,” later revealing he had been taken to a military facility in Nebraska. The year before, when President Bill Clinton visited Pakistan, he descended from an unmarked white plane that had followed Air Force One. His exit, in plain sight, revealed that Clinton had not been on the presidential aircraft.

Footage from July 8 captured by the broadcast press pool shows an airport catering truck pulling up to the side of Air Force One after Trump boarded in Ankara, moments before staff and journalists loaded the same aircraft.
The catering truck pulled away from Air Force One about five minutes after Trump boarded, driving toward the C-32A plane. The truck was parked near the back for four minutes before pulling away.

A press pool note later that day said the flight from Ankara to Mildenhall had been “uneventful,” adding that Trump had not visited the press cabin as he sometimes does. The president was seen deplaning from the jet in Britain, meaning he would have had to sneak back on board Air Force One once at Mildenhall.

NBC News previously reported that a security decision led Trump to take the old Air Force One out of Ankara, a day after the ceasefire with Iran came to an end. The Secret Service urged Trump to fly on the old jet, sources told NBC News in July. The decision was made in consultation with the White House Military Office and the Defense Department. The new plane from Qatar, the sources said, did not have all the security measures that the old one did.

Trump said some days later that the Qatari-gifted plane would be sent away to get “maxed out” for upgrades. That plane, a $400 million Boeing 747, prompted controversy when it was given to him by the Qatari government.

Trump maintained that it would be displayed at his new presidential library in Miami. But last week, the president’s son Eric Trump told NBC News that a different Air Force One will be displayed in the museum, leaving the Qatari plane’s fate uncertain.

title: Jury in Luigi Mangione’s state trial will be anonymous, judge rules
summary: Luigi Mangione appeared Tuesday morning in a New York courtroom where plans were nearly finalized for his state murder trial, which the judge has ruled will have an anonymous jury.
story: Luigi Mangione appeared Tuesday morning in a New York courtroom where plans were nearly finalized for his state murder trial, which the judge has ruled will have an anonymous jury.
Mangione, 28, has pleaded not guilty to several state charges in connection with the December 2024 fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson outside the New York Hilton Midtown.

At Tuesday’s hearing, Justice Gregory Carro ordered the parties to team up on crafting a jury questionnaire — a task that could prove challenging given the case’s notoriety. Jury selection is set to begin Sept. 8, and the trial is expected to last about six weeks.
If convicted, Mangione faces up to life in prison.

It was unclear when the jury questionnaire would be finalized, but Mangione’s side told NBC News that they expect to have a proposed draft this week. The parties are expected to coordinate on a survey that will address each side’s concerns and identify potential jurors who may be biased.

Jurors who make it past the initial screening process will face additional vetting in a process known as voir dire. Questionnaires are designed for the parties and judge to get a preliminary sense of a jury candidate’s background and beliefs.

On Tuesday, the courtroom was filled with journalists and some Mangione proponents, who were wearing green, a color that appeared to reference the Luigi character from the iconic Nintendo Super Mario games and subsequent movies.

Mangione entered the courtroom from a holding area wearing a gray suit. He glanced around the room before taking his seat next to his attorneys, Karen Friedman Agnifilo, Marc Agnifilo and Jacob Kaplan.
Carro ruled at the start of the hearing that the jury would be anonymous, a designation that is becoming increasingly common in high-profile cases in New York.

Carro also said there would be expanded media and public access to the trial. After fielding complaints from Mangione’s defense team about potential space limitations, court administrators arranged for an overflow room.
“It has always been under consideration. They had to find the physical place, and it had to be staffed,” Carro said.
Prior to the conference, the defense and prosecution sparred over how much space would be available for members of the media and public to view the trial.
The defense accused the Manhattan district attorney’s office of unfairly trying to limit the number of attendees, which it argued would also shape the type of coverage that the trial received.
Prosecutors objected to those characterizations but also raised concerns about witness exposure.

“We are particularly concerned about the possibility that a spectator in an overflow room will clandestinely record the proceedings and share any such recordings with others,” prosecutor Joel Seidemann wrote in an Aug. 10 letter.

Seidemann also argued that Mangione supporters have tried to intimidate witnesses and interrupt the jury process, elevating the prosecution’s fears about the “extraordinary pressure on witnesses and potential jurors alike.”
The judge said the district attorney had no role in courtroom access planning and called the defense’s claims of meddling “a reckless mischaracterization.”
Marc Agnifilo, one of Mangione’s lawyers, said outside the courthouse that he was glad the court arranged for extra space.
“I think it actually changed the complexion of the coverage of the trial. ... I think there should be two overflow rooms, but I’ll take one,” Agnifilo said.
Mangione’s case has garnered international headlines, with mostly female supporters who have appeared in court throughout the pretrial hearings and argue that the killing was justified.

Prosecutors allege Mangione was motivated by an animus toward the health insurance industry, but he was never a UnitedHealthcare customer. He had no connection to Thompson, a father of two from Minnesota.
Prosecutors say Mangione trailed Thompson and identified his movements in New York, where the prominent healthcare executive was attending his company’s investors conference.

Prosecutors allege that Mangione shot Thompson from behind outside the hotel, then fled the city. He was apprehended several days later in Altoona, Pennsylvania, after a McDonald’s employee called the police.

Former Manhattan prosecutor Rebecca Roiphe told NBC News that during jury selection, prosecutors will likely want to scrutinize potential jurors’ experiences in the healthcare system to weed out those who might sympathize with Mangione.
“I think the prosecution is clearly going to want to keep off people who have some kind of ax to grind about healthcare,” Roiphe said.
Roiphe, who is a criminal law and ethics professor at New York Law School, believes the defense will seek panelists with a “healthcare-for-all mindset.”

Roiphe said attorneys will also pay close attention to jurors’ attitudes toward law enforcement and politics, even though aspects of Mangione’s case do not seem to strictly apply to a partisan viewpoint.

Mangione separately faces federal stalking-related charges in New York and has pleaded not guilty. The Justice Department was seeking the death penalty in the federal case, but that option was taken off the table earlier this year.
U.S. District Judge Margaret Garnett issued a ruling in January that effectively blocks New York federal prosecutors from pursuing a capital case.

title: Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs chooses former Republican as running mate in re-election bid
summary: Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs has chosen a former Republican as her running mate for her re-election bid this November.
story: Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs has chosen a former Republican as her running mate for her re-election bid this November.
On Tuesday, Hobbs named John Giles, who served as a GOP mayor of Mesa, Arizona, from 2014 to 2025, as her pick for lieutenant governor.
In a joint video announcement with Giles, Hobbs said she has fought for Arizonans as governor by cutting taxes, securing the border and supporting public safety.

“Now, for the first time in our state’s history, we are electing a governor and lieutenant governor on the same ticket. And the first thing I looked for in a running mate was someone who shares that value of putting Arizonans ahead of partisan politics,” Hobbs said.
Giles said, “I was a lifelong Republican before becoming an independent because extremists shouldn’t stand in the way of getting things done.”
Giles changed his party affiliation to independent in May and voted in the Democratic primary last month, Hobbs’ communications director Michael Beyer confirmed to NBC News.
Voters will elect a lieutenant governor for the first time this fall after a ballot measure creating the position was approved in the 2022 election.
The New York Times was first to report on Hobbs’ plans.

Hobbs faces a competitive race against Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., who previously chaired the conservative House Freedom Caucus and has served in Congress since 2017. Biggs has selected former state lawmaker Sine Kerr as his running mate. Biggs won the Republican primary last month, beating fellow Rep. David Schweikert and businessmen Scott Neely and Ken Miceli.

While mayor of Mesa, Giles endorsed then-Vice President Kamala Harris for president in the 2024 election and spoke at the Democratic National Convention in Chicago that year about his disappointment with the Republican Party.

“I’m a lifelong Republican, so I feel a little out of place tonight. But I feel more at home here than in today’s Republican Party,” Giles said in his remarks. “The Grand Old Party has been kidnapped by extremists and devolved into a cult — the cult of Donald Trump.”

He added: “I have an urgent message for the majority of Americans who, like me, are in the political middle. John McCain’s Republican Party is gone, and we don’t owe a damn thing to what’s been left behind.”
The nonpartisan Cook Political Report rated the governor’s race as leaning Democratic in the battleground state, which President Donald Trump carried in 2016 and 2024 and Joe Biden won in 2020.

In 2022, Hobbs defeated Republican Kari Lake in the gubernatorial election by less than 1 percentage point. Before serving as governor, Hobbs was Arizona’s secretary of state. She also has been the minority leader in the state Senate and a member of the state House.
Hobbs recently formed a coalition of former and current Republican and independent leaders who support her re-election, which included Giles and more than 50 other business leaders and officials.

The Democratic incumbent has touted her record of working across the aisle, including signing more than 900 pieces of bipartisan legislation into law, according to her campaign. She has also highlighted her efforts to expand affordable housing and secure the border and her repeal of the state’s 1864 near-total abortion ban.
Biggs, meanwhile, has promoted his relationship with Trump and has run on a campaign touting his support for lowering taxes and border security.

title: Why is the U.S. banning a ton of robot vacuums? Here’s what you should know
summary: The FCC banned foreign-made advanced robots, and robot vacuums fall under the new rules. Here’s what it means for the device you already own — and which models you can still buy.
story: Robots are having a moment with the federal government — and it’s not all positive. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) recently announced a ban on foreign-made advanced mobile robots, a category that covers a ton of different types of robots. And while you probably don’t have a walking, talking robot in your living room yet, you might have something else the ban touches: a robot vacuum.
That everyday cleaning gadget falls squarely into the category now facing new restrictions, and it has nothing to do with battery recalls or overheating parts. Here’s what you need to know.
Why are robot vacuums being banned?

Late last week, the FCC added advanced robotic devices and foreign-made power inverters to its Covered List, the government’s running roster of tech that’s considered too risky to trust. The list flags communications equipment and services the FCC says pose “an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States or the security and safety of United States persons.”

What that means in practice is that anything on the list can’t get FCC equipment authorization. And without that authorization, a product typically can’t be imported, marketed or sold in the United States.

So why robots? According to the FCC’s National Security Determination, it comes down to what these devices can see and record. Robots are often packed with high-tech sensors that are constantly gathering data about the spaces they move through.

The concern isn’t just what the sensors collect, though. It’s also how the devices connect. Because robots typically operate on networks, the FCC notes they’re vulnerable to the same risks as any connected device: getting hacked, having data stolen or even losing control of the device itself.
What is covered under the robot ban?
While the ban seems mostly aimed at humanoid and animal-like robots, the “advanced robotic devices” category casts a much wider net. If a device checks these boxes, it qualifies for the ban,:

It can move, navigate or avoid obstacles on its own.It operates remotely, either through human control or by responding to sensor data.The device (plus any docking station) weighs more than 4.4 pounds combined.It has a sensor that reads its surroundings, can connect to a network at 200 kbps or faster, or runs software — including AI or machine-learning models — that controls how it moves, senses its environment or receives remote commands.
It can move, navigate or avoid obstacles on its own.
It operates remotely, either through human control or by responding to sensor data.
The device (plus any docking station) weighs more than 4.4 pounds combined.

It has a sensor that reads its surroundings, can connect to a network at 200 kbps or faster, or runs software — including AI or machine-learning models — that controls how it moves, senses its environment or receives remote commands.

Sounds like your vacuum, right? That’s because it probably is. Most robot vacuums move around on their own, connect to your Wi-Fi, gather data about your home’s layout and many weigh in above that 4.4-pound threshold. Put it all together, and they check enough boxes to land on the list.

If your robot vacuum is already part of your cleaning routine, take a breath: It’s not going to stop working, and no one’s coming to confiscate it. The ban only applies to new foreign-produced advanced robotic devices — but since so many robot vacuums are made (or built with components made) outside the U.S., that covers the vast majority of what’s currently on the market. The key word there is new. For now, you can still buy any of the existing models that are already available at retailers.
Robot vacuums you can still shop

As mentioned, the existing inventory of robot vacuums in the United States are still up for grabs. With that in mind, I’ve rounded up robot vacuums that are still available to shop today — some are even on sale (at the time of publishing).
Eufy X10 Pro Omni

NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez tested this model as a first-time robot vacuum owner and says it took him just about 15 minutes to understand how everything worked. The robot vacuums and mops, while its base station empties debris, dumps dirty water, refills clean water, dries mop pads and recharges the battery on its own. It also offers advanced navigation, obstacle avoidance, room mapping, no-go zones and customizable routines through the Eufy app.
Lefant Robot Vacuum Cleaner

The Lefant M210 is a compact vacuum built for small spaces and homes with pets. At 11 inches in diameter and less than 3 inches tall, it easily cleans under beds, sofas and other low furniture. Instead of a traditional roller brush, it uses a suction port that pulls in pet hair and dirt without the tangling that roller brushes are prone to. It also offers six cleaning modes, infrared sensors to navigate around furniture and avoid falls, and app, Alexa or Google Assistant controls. When the battery runs low, it automatically returns to its charging dock, making it a low-maintenance option for everyday upkeep.
Roborock Q7 L5 Robot Vacuum

The Roborock Q7 L5 vacuums and mops your floors at the same time, using strong suction to pull dirt out of carpets and crevices while a laser mapping system helps it find the most efficient path around your home. It’s built with anti–tangle brushes meant to resist hair wrapping, so you don’t have to clean them out as often, and the mop pads can clean dried-on stains from floors. You can use the app to set cleaning schedules and pick which rooms the vac should avoid.
iRobot Roomba 105 Vac Robot Vacuum

The iRobot Roomba 105 Vac cleans your floors on its own, using much stronger suction than older Roomba models, plus a brush along the edges and a main brush pick up different kinds of dirt. It uses laser mapping to scan and remember the layout of your home, so it can clean more thoroughly instead of bumping around randomly. You can control it through an app, which lets you schedule cleanings, focus on specific rooms and skip others.

What is a hair rinse?

A hair rinse is a liquid treatment you’ll usually use after shampooing to address hair or scalp concerns, such as buildup, dullness, or scalp imbalance. You pour or spray the rinse over your hair and scalp, let it sit briefly and then rinse out. What makes hair rinses stand out is their consistency and contact time: “Rinses are thin, they move through the hair quickly, and they are designed to make a chemical adjustment rather than deposit a lot of product,” says Harris-Burke.

Unlike shampoo, which cleanses, or conditioner, which moisturizes and detangles, a hair rinse provides an additional targeted benefit; some rinses focus on the scalp, while others improve the look and feel of your hair shaft, says Foad.

“A hair rinse is more of a supportive product,” says Parikh. “It can help remove buildup, rebalance the scalp or improve the condition of the hair itself. It’s not a treatment for hair loss, but maintaining a healthy scalp creates a better environment for healthy hair over time.”
What are the different types of hair rinses?

There are multiple types of hair rinses, each serving a different purpose. “It’s less about choosing the trendiest product and more about choosing the one that addresses your specific scalp or hair concerns,” says Parikh.
These are the four main types of hair rinses, according to experts:

Acidic rinses (pH balancing): These have acids like citric, lactic or glycolic to lower your hair’s pH after shampooing and help lay the cuticle flat, making it appear shinier, says Harris. Acidic rinses are best for anyone with high-porosity hair, especially those with frizz, dullness or breakage. “This is the most universally useful category,” says Harris.Vinegar rinses: You’ll often see these as apple cider vinegar rinses, which have acetic acid. “They lower pH, dissolve buildup and get rid of hard water minerals,” says Harris. They’re best for people dealing with heavy product buildup, hard water or an oily, congested scalp. The trade-off is the strong smell, and the acidity means you’ll need to dilute it properly and use it less frequently, experts say.Glosses and glazes: These are semi-permanent cuticle treatments that add shine and, in tinted versions, deposit temporary color. They’re great if your hair looks dull or if you want to refresh your color between salon visits, says Harris. Clear or sheer versions give you the shine benefit without any color change, which makes them a great option for natural hair.Herbal and botanical rinses: This is the gentlest hair rinse category and the one you can typically use more frequently. They’re usually infused with rosemary, nettle, horsetail, chamomile, hibiscus, green tea or rice water, and they work to support your scalp and soothe irritation. Herbal and botanical rinses are also great for those with sensitive scalps who can’t tolerate an acidic rinse.

Herbal and botanical rinses are also great for those with sensitive scalps who can’t tolerate an acidic rinse.
What are the benefits of hair rinses for different hair types?
Most hair rinses are great for any hair type, as long as you’re using the proper one for your specific concerns. Here are a few common hair types and how each benefits from a hair rinse:

Color-treated hair: Choose carefully. Strong vinegar and clarifying rinses can pull color and make it fade faster, so consider a gentle acidic rinse and gloss instead. “Glosses in particular can extend the life of your color between appointments,” says Harris.Dry, damaged hair: Acidic rinses are especially useful. “Damaged hair has a compromised cuticle that sits raised, so a pH-lowering rinse makes a visible difference,” says Harris. “Just avoid over-clarifying because damaged hair has less margin for error.”Curly and coily hair: This hair type usually benefits the most from clarifying hair rinses. “Textured hair is prone to buildup from gels, creams and butters, and buildup is one of the main reasons curls stop clumping and defining well,” says Harris. “A clarifying or chelating rinse every few weeks can reset your hair. The critical rule is to always follow with a deep conditioner because textured hair cannot afford to be stripped.”Locs: Rinses are useful for buildup, but rinse thoroughly and dry completely afterward, says Harris.

The critical rule is to always follow with a deep conditioner because textured hair cannot afford to be stripped.”

What are the best ingredients to look for in a hair rinse?
Here are the most effective ingredients to consider for the most common hair and scalp concerns, according to Harris:

For product buildup and hard water: acetic acid, citric acid and glycolic acid.For dullness and lack of shine: citric acid, lactic acid and cationic conditioning agents like behentrimonium chloride or cetrimonium chloride, which help close the cuticle and make hair softer.For an itchy, flaky scalp: tea tree oil, salicylic acid, willow bark extract and zinc pyrithione. If flaking continues, that’s a sign to see a professional rather than keep switching products.For thinning hair: rosemary extract, peppermint, caffeine and niacinamide. “Rosemary in particular has some of the more encouraging research behind it, though I always frame it as scalp support rather than a cure,” says Harris. However, it’s important to have realistic expectations: “These products can support healthy hair and scalp care, but they’re not substitutes for evidence-based treatments when someone is experiencing true hair loss,” says Parikh.For dryness and porosity: panthenol, glycerin, aloe, hydrolyzed rice or wheat protein, and amino acids.

For thinning hair: rosemary extract, peppermint, caffeine and niacinamide. “Rosemary in particular has some of the more encouraging research behind it, though I always frame it as scalp support rather than a cure,” says Harris. However, it’s important to have realistic expectations: “These products can support healthy hair and scalp care, but they’re not substitutes for evidence-based treatments when someone is experiencing true hair loss,” says Parikh.
For dryness and porosity: panthenol, glycerin, aloe, hydrolyzed rice or wheat protein, and amino acids.

Those with color-treated hair should look for labels like “color-safe” and “sulfate-free.” Most people with color-treated hair prefer glosses or gentle acidic rinses over strong vinegar formulas, says Harris
Frequently asked questions

While the benefits of a hair rinse depend on its ingredients, they can usually help remove buildup from your shampoo or other styling products, smooth the hair cuticle to increase shine, make your strands more manageable and support a healthier scalp environment, says Foad. Some rinses also help rebalance the scalp’s pH after cleansing, which may reduce irritation and leave hair looking smoother.
You can think of using a hair rinse almost like cleaning your kitchen, says Christine McMillan, a board-certified trichologist and owner of Scalp Garden.

“Shampoo is like washing the dishes: Its entire job is to get rid of grease, dirt and leftovers. Conditioner is like putting oil on your wooden cutting board so it stays smooth and doesn’t dry out. A hair mask is like deep conditioning that cutting board overnight; it’s meant to do more heavy lifting versus everyday maintenance,” says McMillan. “A rinse is different and more like a specialty cleaner. Maybe you’re trying to remove hard water spots, polish stainless steel or disinfect a countertop. Hair rinses are designed to do one particular job after shampooing. Some focus on your hair, some your scalp, and some do a little of both.”

In most cases, you should use a hair rinse alongside a conditioner rather than replacing it. “A rinse may help clarify the scalp or smooth the hair, but it doesn’t typically provide the level of hydration, lubrication or detangling that a conditioner does,” says Foad. “If your hair is very fine, you may find that certain hydrating rinses are sufficient on occasion, but most people benefit from using both.”
Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to correctly use a hair rinse, according to Harris:
Shampoo first. “A rinse works best on clean hair because applying it over dirt and product means it spends its energy on the residue instead of your hair,” says Harris.
Squeeze out excess water. Soaking wet hair dilutes the rinse and reduces its effectiveness.

Apply strategically. For scalp-specific rinses, use an applicator bottle with a nozzle tip to apply it, which lets you part your hair and get the product directly on your scalp where you need it, says Harris. If your rinse is made for strands, pour or spray from the mid-shaft to your ends and work it through with your fingers.

Follow the directions carefully. “Most rinses need two to five minutes. Longer is not better, especially with acidic formulas,” says Harris. “Also, if the label tells you to dilute, dilute, and do not eyeball it. Concentration matters.”
Rinse with cool water. Cool water helps the cuticle close, locking in the smoothing effect.
Follow your rinse with a conditioner unless the product specifies otherwise.

If you’re experiencing significant scalp irritation, persistent itching, painful scalp lesions, excessive hair shedding or a diagnosed scalp condition, you should speak with a dermatologist before trying any new treatments, says Foad. “These symptoms may indicate an underlying medical condition that requires evaluation rather than simply changing hair care products,” she says.

You can, and people have been doing it for generations using ingredients like rice water, apple cider vinegar, rosemary tea, hibiscus and aloe. However, there are a few concerns. A homemade herbal or rice water rinse is a growing medium for bacteria and mold, so make small batches, refrigerate them, use them within a few days, and never keep a batch sitting on your shelf, says Harris. There is also very little consistency: “You don’t know the actual pH of what you mixed, which makes it hard to troubleshoot when something goes wrong,” says Harris.

Dilution is extremely important, and undiluted apple cider vinegar on the scalp is far too acidic and can cause irritation and cuticle damage, says Harris. If you insist on a DIY journey, a safe starting point is one to two tablespoons of apple cider vinegar in about sixteen ounces of water, she says.

Fermented rice water is a very popular DIY option right now, but you should tread carefully. “Overuse can leave hair stiff and protein overloaded, and low porosity hair is the most vulnerable to that,” says Harris. “This is also the DIY that takes the most work since traditional fermentation runs for days before the batch is usable.”

title: Family of NYC fashion designer found dead on Montauk boat to file wrongful death lawsuit
summary: The family of a New York City fashion designer found dead on a boat in the Hamptons last year is preparing to file a wrongful death lawsuit against the man she was with when she died.
story: The family of a New York City fashion designer found dead on a boat in the Hamptons last year is preparing to file a wrongful death lawsuit against the man she was with when she died.
Martha Nolan-O’Slatarra, 33, was found dead on a boat owned by Christopher Durnan, 61, and docked at the Montauk Yacht Club in the ritzy region of New York’s Long Island on Aug. 5 of last year.

Her family filed a summons with notice against Durnan in Manhattan Supreme Court last week, accusing him of assault, gross negligence, and reckless and wanton conduct in connection with Nolan-O’Slatarra’s death. The family is seeking a sum of $50 million in damages. Durnan has not been charged with any crimes in connection with the death.

A lawyer for Nolan-O’Slatarra’s family, Michael Bowe of Brithem LLP, said in a statement to NBC News that the family has conducted their own investigation of Nolan-O’Slatarra’s death and “does not believe Martha died from intoxicants.”
He said that EMTs found “blood in her mouth, on her chest and head, on the floor, and possibly behind her head” and reported “the body was cold despite her allegedly having just lost consciousness.”

Durnan did not immediately return a request for comment. An attorney for Durnan, Robert Holdman, told New York Magazine last year that his client was “absolutely destroyed” over Nolan-O’Slatarra’s death.
“He watched his friend die in trauma,” the lawyer said.
The Suffolk County Medical Examiner has not publicly released a final cause and manner of death for Nolan-O’Slatarra. The examiner’s office did not immediately return a request for comment.

The Suffolk County Police Department issued a statement in the days following Nolan-O’Slatarra’s death saying that her autopsy “did not show evidence of violence and her final cause of death is pending further examination.”
The police department declined to comment on the discrepancy between their statement and the new allegations.
East Hampton Town Police responded to a 911 call from a man reporting a woman unconscious on a boat docked around midnight the day she was pronounced dead, according to last year’s statement.
She was pronounced dead on the boat by first responders after good samaritans attempted to perform CPR on her, police said.

Nolan-O’Slatarra was originally from Ireland and owned a swimwear company East x East. She said in a 2024 interview with the Irish Independent that she came to New York to follow her dreams as a businesswoman.

“I was the small town girl who needed to get out to achieve her big dreams,” she said. “I always knew I wanted to be successful, that I was money-driven, business-driven — and that fashion is a tough industry and it would be a slow road.”

title: Sugarland Is Taking Breakout Album ‘Enjoy the Ride’ Back on Tour for 20th Anniversary
summary: Sugarland is hitting the road for their “Ride Or Die Tour” for a very special reason: the 20th anniversary of their breakout album “Enjoy the Ride.”
story: Sugarland is hitting the road for a very special reason.
To celebrate the 20th anniversary of their hit album “Enjoy the Ride,” the country duo is heading out on tour this fall.

On Aug. 11, Jennifer Nettles and Kristian Bush sat down with Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones to discuss their exciting announcement and give a preview of what fans can expect from the aptly named the “Ride Or Die Tour.”

Nettles and Bush will be touring cities across the country from Oct. 1 to Nov. 21 to celebrate the album that solidified their spot as country icons. The official Instagram account for the duo released the official lineup of dates Aug. 11. Ticket presale begins Aug. 12 at 10 a.m. followed by general onsale Aug. 14.

Following its 2006 release, “Enjoy the Ride” went triple platinum. Throughout their time as a band, Sugarland has sold nearly 10 million albums in the U.S. The duo has won two Grammy Awards,  five ACM Awards and five consecutive CMA Awards for vocal duo of the year, from 2007 to 2011.
Nettles specifically points to “Enjoy the Ride” as a “turning point” in their career.
“Our debut album was great, but then this (was) really like when people started to really catch on to what we were doing and like it,” she said.

Bush said the album holds a special place in Sugarland’s heart since it was the first one they produced together. Outside of the band, Bush himself has produced an endless amount of music for other artists.
“Dreaming up how things sound and how they feel, it’s something I’ve been doing my whole life,” he said.
Looking back on their band’s enduring success, Nettles said she has “so much gratitude,” and Bush echoed her sentiments.
After collaborating for several decades, Bush and Nettles have a simple secret for forming a successful working relationship that lasts.

“I think like any relationship, you keep it fresh and you communicate. It doesn’t matter if it’s family. It doesn’t matter if it’s intimate. It doesn’t matter if it’s creative. Whatever, like keep it fresh. We do obviously other things. Kristian’s a fantastic producer (and) has hit records out the wazoo with Megan Moroney right now,” Nettles said.
Bush added that he and Nettles are a “unique duo” for one particular reason.

“Almost every single time we’ve sat down to do anything, maybe even in the dressing room before we walked up here, we will come up with ideas on the spot that work almost every time. And I don’t know what that (is), you know, I grab onto her,” he said.

Before announcing their new tour, Sugarland teased some exciting news on their Instagram account, posting a video of the country duo taking a bow on stage. The band captioned the post, “It’s been a minute...” and added the words “Coming soon” to the end of the video.

The day before announcing their tour, Sugarland shared another video of Nettles and Bush performing. As a plethora of excited fan comments appeared in the video, the words “We hear you!” could be seen at the end of the short clip.
Sugarland added fuel to the fire, captioning the post, “Don’t miss out...”

Sugarland released their last album in 2018 with “Bigger,” reuniting after going on hiatus starting in 2012. Nettles and Bush last toured together as Sugarland in 2024, co-headlining the “Take Me Home Tour” with Little Big Town.

title: QVC’s Toni Brattin Says She ‘Froze’ After That Viral Mishap: ‘I Just Went Down!’
summary: Jimmy Fallon had a visit from QVC wig mogul Tami Brattin days after her viral moment.
story: Jimmy Fallon’s comedic take on a viral QVC on-air moment has viewers wigging out.
The host of “The Tonight Show” welcomed TV personality Toni Brattin to his show Aug. 10 and spoofed an embarrassing moment she experienced during a recent QVC segment.
In case you missed the hilarious moment, Brattin was showcasing her collection of wigs on air when she accidentally made a NSFW reference.
While describing the wig she was wearing, Brattin said, “It looks like you went and got a blowjob.” She quickly self-corrected, saying, “a blowout at your salon.”
Terri Conn, a QVC host who was also present for the segment, quickly intervened and reminded viewers that they could take advantage of a “huge beauty sale.”
As Conn began to speak, Brattin shook her head and lowered herself to the floor, out of the camera frame.

After viewing the awkward on-air moment, Fallon poked fun at it during an episode of “The Tonight Show” last week, saying, “Note to all the married men out there: The wig is only available on your birthday, apparently.”
When Brattin saw the clip, she applauded Fallon for his witty comment during an interview with TMZ.

“Jimmy, hat’s off. I had to laugh at him as much as I had to laugh at myself. I happened to save one of those wigs just for Jimmy and I would love to see what this wig would look like on Jimmy. So Jimmy, you just tell me when your birthday is and I’ll hand deliver this and we’ll see how cute you look in it,” she said.
Brattin kept her promise and appeared on “The Tonight Show” Aug. 10.
Fallon set the scene for the segment, saying, “My birthday is actually coming up.”
Brattin then appeared and waved a brown wig in the air.
“I think that you handled that perfectly, by the way. You really nailed it,” Fallon told Brattin of her viral moment.
The TV host then asked the QVC personality what she was thinking as she slowly sank out of the camera frame after her on-air flub.
“Well, you know, I was kind of froze(n) and I was trying to decide, ‘Do I go to the left? Do I go to the right?’ I just went down,” she said.
Brattin then showed Fallon the brown wig she selected for him and put it on his head.
“Oh, look at all that hair!” she said.
“Yeah, you love it?” Fallon replied.
“And how about the volume in the back?” she added.
“Oh yeah. I love it,” Fallon said, then posed. “I’m honored. I love it.”
Brattin paused to fluff up the wig a bit then covered her face and laughed as Fallon exclaimed, “I am blown away.”
The duo ended the segment by turning their backs to the camera and lowering their bodies as they introduced “The Tonight Show” house band, The Roots.

title: Usher Responds to Rumors as Fans Believe He’s Hired a Look-Alike to Perform at Concerts
summary: Usher is shutting down rumors that he’s been sending out an imposter to perform in his place during his recent joint tour with Chris Brown.
story: Usher is shutting down rumors that he’s been sending out an imposter to perform in his place during his recent joint tour with Chris Brown.
Fans have been doing double takes for days after footage from a recent “The R&B Tour” concert has convinced many of them that the man performing on stage was a fake.

Sunnya Sultan, who saw the tour in person Aug. 7 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, shared a TikTok video questioning if the 47-year-old “Yeah” singer was truly the one dancing in front of her.
The performer wears a white with lime green and pink ensemble, ball cap and sunglasses as he sings and dances.
Sultan tells TODAY.com she believes she did see Usher perform. She’s also convinced an Usher look-alike also took the stage during a portion of the show.

“Usher came out. The real Usher came out but then he sang like half a song, maybe for like 40 seconds,” Sultan recalls. “Then he goes into this darkness and he comes out, and as he’s walking, I think everyone really thought that was Usher.”
“But as the first song finishes, I think everyone started getting confused because the way he was moving wasn’t really Usher,” she continues.

When she looked closely, she believed something was off about the Usher who now appeared onstage. She noted that his jawline that was “a little too chiseled” and the performer “seemed a little too stiff.”
Also, he was dressed differently. The “real” Usher, she says, came out shirtless and wearing a fur coat.
The Usher who later performed in front of her, she adds, was “fully covered,” as seen in her TikTok video.
“Everything was just kind of weird,” Sultan says. “He looked like him, and then at certain angles he definitely did not look like him.”
Sultan said concertgoers all around her were suspicious.
Usher addressed the rumors in a video posted on the tour’s official Instagram Aug. 9.
“Usure? Wesure,” reads the caption.
The video showed Usher performing onstage in the same white ensemble. It also included screenshots of Usher replying to comments made about the alleged imposter.
“Ya’ll are funny…clone? They can’t clone this??” the singer wrote alongside a laughing emoji.
“How ya’ll come up with this? AI ain’t that advanced,” he added along with more laughing emoji.

title: ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Has Shocking Elimination After Dancer Failed to Deliver ‘Wow Moment’
summary: Who was eliminated on ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ episode 5? The Aug. 10 episode saw a shocking elimination after one dancer failed to deliver a “wow moment.”
story: The competition continues on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” and now it’s time to shine.
In the Aug. 10 episode of the “Dancing With the Stars” spinoff, pro Daniella Karagach showed off her impressive skills with a mega performance as host Robert Irwin introduced the challenge.

This week it was all about having that “wow” moment that “DWTS” viewers love. The six remaining dancers were mentored and guided by Daniella as they created a contemporary routine that incorporated one of her signature and viral moves.
If the dancers failed to deliver a spectacular move in their choreographer, they would be at risk for elimination. But first, the contestants took a trip to the Australia Zoo for inspiration.
What Happened During Episode 5 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’

When Daniella entered the rehearsal room, she told the dancers that they also had to create their own standout moment that would “forever be embedded in someone’s memory.” This was in addition to including one of Daniella’s “wow” moves.
“The more you wow the audience, the longer you and your partner stay in the competition,” she said about competing on “DWTS.”

Since last week, the ladies got to choose their partners, this week the guys picked who they wanted to perform with. If more than one guy chose the same girl, she would have the option to choose who she wanted to partner up with.
Allen Genkin chose Adele Zaikman, while AJ Pritchard and Erik Linder chose Selena Hamilton. No one chose Nina Mayster.
Selena ultimately chose Erik, meaning AJ and Nina would be partners by default.

AJ and Nina were up first, performing a contemporary piece to “Human” by Christina Perri that impressed the judges. Daniella told them they “understood the assignment,” while judge Mark Ballas complimented their “total trust.”
Shirley Ballas also applauded their multiple wow moments, AJ’s vulnerability and Nina’s musicality.
Next were Allen and Adele, who also got major kudos from the judges with their routine to “All That Really Matters” by Illenium featuring Teddy Swims.
Mark was a fan of their wow moments, that included the Allen-copter and caveman walk at the beginning. He also called Adele a “diamond.”
Shirley echoed her son’s comments, calling her “beyond a diamond, one of the best female dancers I’ve ever seen.” Daniella also shared how she loved the routine.
Last but not least were Erik and Selena, who specializes in contemporary, with a routine to “You Stole the Show” by Sienna Spiro.
Shirley began her comments by saying she was “conflicted” and didn’t know what their wow moment was. Selena replied that sometimes the “wow” is in the silence.
Shirley continued by saying she would have liked to see Erik let go more and ultimately wasn’t impressed. While she did appreciate the quality of Selena’s routine, she expected more.
Mark and Daniella both shared kind words about their dancing, but noted that they did not follow direction.
Who Was in the Bottom 2?
Because they did not complete the challenge and include a visibly “wow moment” in their routine, Erik and Selena were on the chopping block.
The other four contestants were visibly emotional in the background, as Daniella said, “If you have a challenge, you have to deliver it. You have to make that the priority.”
Who Got Eliminated on Episode 5 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’?
Ultimately, Shirley shared that with a “very, very heavy heart” this would be the last dance for Erik.
Allen broke down in tears, with Adele and Nina covering their faces in shock.
Shirley told Erik that he was “a beautiful dancer,” but applauded Selena for her strong and advanced choreography.

“I knew that I was taking a risk,” Erik said in his confessional, adding that he didn’t regret a single decision that he made. He then thanked the judges for the opportunity to grow as a dancer and person.
What Will Happen Next Week?
Five dancers remain on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro.” For the Aug. 17 episode, guest judge Witney Carson will deliver the dancers’ toughest challenge yet: teaching ballroom novice.
In the next episode, the contestants will be paired with “DWTS” superfans who are dancing amateurs. They will then have two days to prepare a performance that will land them a spot in the semifinals.

title: Brad Pitt Makes Rare Comment About ‘Pain’ of ‘Family Stuff’
summary: In a new interview, Brad Pitt shares that he’s never been suicidal “except for one little period” that was related to “family stuff.”
story: This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. You can also text HOME to 741741 or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional resources.
In a rare mention of his personal life, Brad Pitt says in a new interview that he has never been suicidal “except for one little period” that was related to “family stuff.”

The 62-year-old Hollywood icon made a short reference to his family situation in an interview with Esquire published on Aug. 10  in which he talked about “oppressive” pain that led him to a dark place where he could “understand suicide.”
In the Esquire interview, Pitt initially shared his thoughts about going to dark places in life, unconnected to any question about his family.
“I was never suicidal in any way,” he said. “It just was not my makeup. In fact, if I have any afflictions, it’s probably being a congenital optimist,” he said.
He reiterated he’s “never been suicidal,” before adding, “except for one little period.”

“And in that one little period, I just thought — I just couldn’t — just didn’t see a way out,” he said. “The pain was so oppressive that — I wasn’t going to act on this, but I could feel — I could feel the cold steel of the bullet in my head, and it felt like relief. And I thought, Oh, okay, now I understand — I understand suicide, in the sense that it’s just relief. It’s just looking for relief from the pain. But I also think we have incredible survival instincts. And for me, that immediately kicked in, but it was just ...”
Pitt was asked what could have provoked him to think about suicide in that way. The reporter questioned if it was “kid stuff,” per the Esquire article.
“Family stuff,” Pitt said. “We could leave it at that.”

Pitt and his ex-wife, Angelina Jolie, have six children. The couple reached a divorce settlement in 2024 after Jolie accused Pitt of verbal and physical abuse, which he has denied. Their daughter Shiloh, 20, legally dropped “Pitt” from her last name when she turned 18 in 2024. Two of his other children have also considered ditching “Pitt” from their last name, according to a court filing in California cited by CNN in July 2026.
The “F1” star was later asked how he endured the difficult period he referenced.

“I don’t see it as climbing out of it,” he said. “It’s going through it and trying and trying and trying and trying to the point of exhaustion and then trying again. I don’t want to ignore the place where you run up against the wall. But I just one day woke up, and it just felt a little sunnier and the air felt a little sweeter. Just microdoses of it.”

Pitt does not make it clear in the interview what “little period” he is referring to in his life. Elsewhere in the interview, he discussed the death of his mother in August 2025 and said, referencing his father, “Let’s just say it’s better to be the one who goes first.”
Once Hollywood’s most famous couple, Pitt, and Jolie, 51, met on the set of the 2005 movie “Mr. & Mrs. Smith” and got married in 2014. Jolie filed for divorce in 2016.

In 2022, amid already contentious divorce proceedings, Jolie accused Pitt of physical and verbal abuse on a 2016 flight from France to Los Angeles, during which he allegedly choked one of their children, which prompted her to file for divorce, according to a court filing from Jolie.
“Brad has owned everything he’s responsible for from day one — unlike the other side — but he’s not going to own anything he didn’t do,” a lawyer for Pitt said in 2022.

No criminal charges were ever filed against Pitt. In 2016, both the FBI and the Los Angeles County Department of Children and Family Services closed an investigation into allegations of abuse onboard the flight.

The acrimony since their split has also included Pitt filing a lawsuit in 2022 accusing Jolie of intentionally harming him and the French winery business they once shared by selling her stake in it. The former couple purchased shares in the 148-acre French vineyard Chateau Miraval together in 2008.

Following Pitt’s lawsuit about the winery, Jolie filed the 2022 cross-complaint that alleged Pitt subjected their family to verbal and physical abuse aboard the aforementioned 2016 flight from France to Los Angeles.
Their divorce was settled in 2024, and the dispute over the winery remains ongoing.

title: Romy Reiner’s Latest TV Role Has a Touching Tie to Her Late Dad, Rob Reiner
summary: Romy Reiner appeared in the finale of Larry David’s “Life, Larry, and the Pursuit of Unhappiness,” which her dad Rob Reiner also appeared in.
story: Romy Reiner followed in her late father Rob Reiner’s footsteps by appearing on Larry David’s “Life, Larry, and the Pursuit of Unhappiness.”
The elder Reiner made a posthumous cameo in the sketch show in an episode that aired July 3, months after his shocking death. He played George Washington.
Romy Reiner, meanwhile, guest-starred in the series finale on Aug. 7 as a nurse caring for President William Henry Harrison (Fred Melamed).
Romy Reiner’s appearance comes five years after she got her big break in 2021 playing a cashier on David’s HBO series “Curb Your Enthusiasm.” David was one of Rob Reiner’s close friends.
The 28-year-old actor is the youngest child of the legendary actor and director and his late wife Michele Singer.
The couple, who were married for 36 years, were found fatally stabbed at home on Dec. 14, 2025, according to the L.A. district attorney’s office.
Their youngest son, Nick Reiner, 32, was arrested and charged Dec. 16 with two counts of first degree murder. In February, Nick Reiner pleaded not guilty to the charges.
The Reiners also shared an older son, Jake Reiner, 35, who posted a heartbreaking tribute to his parents in an April 24 post on Substack.
Rob Reiner was also the father of an adoptive daughter, Tracy Reiner, with his ex-wife, actor and director Penny Marshall.
In his essay on Substack, Jake Reiner revealed he was at a friend’s celebration of life in Los Angeles when his sister called to tell him their parents were dead.
